items.title: [RFC]: Online quantization from arbitrary precision
items.author: fxmarty-amd
items.body_excerpt:
### Motivation.

This RFC is ported from wider https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167.

We propose to extend online quantization API to allow re-quantization from arbitrary weight original precision (arbitrary weight quant key), not only `BF16/FP16/FP32`. `FP8 -> MXFP4` re-quantization in vLLM should STILL be considered online quantization. Same as `NVFP4 -> MXFP4`, or anything else.

**Motivations:**
- No reason to treat BF16/FP16/FP32 in a privileged fashion in online quantization, many models are now released in lower precision and it is useful to enable conversion in-framework for quick experimentation on accuracy / speed impact.
- Widen oracle usage (do not hack given precision oracle into handling other precision)
- More flexibility to convert to:
    - Higher precision if given hardware does not support lower precision.
    - Lower/same precision/variant if given hardware supports it (e.g. NVFP4 -> MXFP4, FP8 -> MXFP4). 

Example usage:

```bash
vllm serve mmangkad/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-MXFP8 --quantization-config.linear "fp8_per_channel"
```

This involves supporting weight loading from existing quant method classes, and conversion to online quant methods. This is showcased in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55684.

This has e.g. been requested in:
- `MXFP8` to `FP8 PTPC`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427
- `MXFP4` to `INT4`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51274 (targeting gfx942 kernel)

Taking the example of `MXFP4 -> INT4` conversion, I believe we should make use of online quantization API for this kind of feature, where eventually INT4 oracle is used and NOT MXFP4 oracle, as the eventual weight format has nothing to do anymore with MXFP4, and any `quant key -> INT4` can then re-use the very same INT4 oracle.

The eventual actual weight quant key (post-conversion) oracle should thus handle the backend dispatch and post-processing, not the original checkpoint quant key oracle.

Long term, it should make maintainability a lot easier to maintain a clear separation between:

- model producers (Quark/modelopt/compressed-tensors/mxfp4/fp8) / quant method classes handling **loading only**,
- Online quant methods / online quantization API handling weight keys if weights are re-quantized,
- Oracles handling different weight key (that should hopefully be unified as per https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37753), including weight key after conversion,
- MOE/linear backends handling specific weight key, and dispatched to by their oracle.

Note: this feature is similar to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28291 & https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29328 on sglang side.


### Proposed Change.

Changes in: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55684. Note how lightweight the proposed implementation is:

```python
    def dequantize_weight(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Reconstruct serialized weights for online requantization."""
        if self.wkey.key is kMxfp8Static:
            # NOTE: dequantize method could directly be attached to QuantKey as well.
            return dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16(
                layer.weight.contiguous(), layer.weight_scale.contiguous()
            )
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                "ModelOpt weight dequantization is only supported for MXFP8."
            )
```

that is completely optional, as the base `QuantizeMethodBase` defines:

```python
    def dequantize_weight(self, layer: nn.Module) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Materialize a serialized quantized weight for requantization."""
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"The quantization method {type(self)} does not implement "
            "dequantize_weight. Please open an issue."
        )
```


### Feedback Period.

2 weeks

### CC List.

_No response_

### Any Other Things.

Related topics (oracle usage):
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37753
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54959

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [MP][ROCm][Bug] L1 pinned via hipHostRegister stays movable: compaction triggers KFD queue eviction, MP server freezes 30–79 s
items.author: stefanskiasan
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

On ROCm, `LazyMemoryAllocator` pins L1 via `cudaHostRegister` (→ `hipHostRegister`), which becomes a KFD **userptr** mapping. The pages stay **movable**, so `VmPin` stays at 0 and the kernel is still free to migrate them. With a large L1 on a host with little free memory, direct compaction keeps migrating L1 pages. Every migration fires the MMU notifier. KFD then evicts **all user queues of the MP server process on every visible GPU** and revalidates the userptr BOs while holding the process's `mmap_lock`.

While that lasts, every page fault in the server blocks, the ZMQ I/O thread included. The whole MP server freezes for **30–79 s**. All connected vLLM workers log `LMCache server is unhealthy — entering degraded mode` in the same millisecond, and with `kv_load_failure_policy=fail` the in-flight requests fail.

## Environment

- 8× AMD Instinct MI350X, ROCm/HIP 7.2.53211, amdgpu 6.16.13, Linux 6.8.0 (Ubuntu), 2.3 TB RAM
- LMCache 0.5.4, MP server (`lmcache server … --l1-size-gb 1200 --l1-init-size-gb 64 --supported-transfer-mode lmcache_driven`), one server shared by two vLLM TP4 instances
- L1 = 1200 GB via `LazyMemoryAllocator` (64 MB `PIN_CHUNK_SIZE`, ~19k registrations); host page cache ~850 GB, `MemFree` ~20 GB
- THP `enabled=madvise`, `defrag=madvise`, `vm.compaction_proactiveness=20` (distro defaults)

## Evidence

1. Server log: single transfers suddenly take tens of seconds (normally ~0.05 s), identical on all TP ranks:
   ```
   Retrieved 256 tokens in 58.194 seconds
   Stored 8192 tokens in 72.317 seconds
   ```
2. `/sys/class/kfd/kfd/proc/<server-pid>/stats_*/evicted_ms` (readable without root): **922 s** of queue eviction in 8 h for the MP server, versus ~20 s for the vLLM workers.
3. A 2 s sampler of `/proc/vmstat` + `evicted_ms` shows the correlation directly:
   | time (UTC) | compact_stall Δ | pgmigrate_success Δ | evicted_ms afterwards |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | 19:53:53 | 267 | 38,930 | +47 s |
   | 19:54:49–51 | 1,078 | 211,587 | +28 s |

   `compact_daemon_wake` stayed at 0, so the migrations came from **direct** compaction, not from kcompactd.
4. Kernel stack of a server thread during the freeze:
   ```
   ZMQbg/IO/0 state=D
     lock_mm_and_find_vma
     do_user_addr_fault
     exc_page_fault
     _copy_to_iter
     skb_copy_datagram_iter
   ```

## Fix we run in production

`mlock()` each chunk right before `cudaHostRegister` in `LazyMemoryAllocator._pin_memory_chunk`, and set `vm.compact_unevictable_allowed=0` so that compaction skips mlocked pages. `mlock` alone is not enough, because the default `=1` still lets compaction migrate them.

```python
# lazy_memory_allocator.py, _pin_memory_chunk, before current_device_spec.pin_memory(ptr, size, 2)
if _libc.mlock(ctypes.c_void_p(ptr), ctypes.c_size_t(size)) != 0:
    logger.warning("mlock failed for chunk at ptr=%#x size=%d: errno %d", ptr, size, ctypes.get_errno())
```

The container also needs `--ulimit memlock=-1:-1` (or `CAP_IPC_LOCK`). Server start takes ~2.5 min longer because the initial 64 GB get faulted in. We additionally set `vm.compaction_proactiveness=0` and THP `defrag=defer`.

Result over 33 h of production: `VmLck` = full 1.2 TB, KFD eviction **2.4 s** total (was 922 s per 8 h), longest transfer 1.2 s (was 72 s), 0 `unhealthy` events, 0 failed requests. The kernel still did 4.2 M migrations and 2.3 k compaction stalls in that time; they just no longer touch L1.

## Suggestions

- ROCm: optionally `mlock` pinned L1 chunks (e.g. a config flag, default on for ROCm) and log a warning when `vm.compact_unevictable_allowed != 0`, or allocate L1 with `hipHostMalloc` (driver-owned GTT, not movable) instead of registering user memory.
- Document the `memlock` ulimit / sysctl requirement for large L1 on ROCm.
- It would also help if the heartbeat logged individual ping failures. #4670 makes the same point: our 40–79 s windows were only visible as enter/leave transitions.

Happy to open a PR for the `mlock` option if that direction is acceptable.

items.title: [Bug]: TENT remote NIC selection can pair a rail NIC with a peer NIC it cannot reach; each such pair costs an RC retry timeout before the rail is paused
items.author: xiaodouzi666
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

**What happens**

`Workers::selectOptimalDevice` picks the remote device from the rail mapping (`findBestRemoteDevice`, by position/NUMA) or from the target's device list at a random start, preferring the same NUMA node (`src/transport/rdma/workers.cpp:1540-1590`, as of `342c8aee`). Nothing in the selection asks whether the local and the remote NIC are on networks that reach each other. On hosts with a front-end NIC (`mlx5_0`, overlay network) and four rail NICs (separate rail subnets), with all five NICs enabled on both sides, the selector pairs a rail NIC with the peer's `mlx5_0`: the QP's RC retries exhaust after ~3.7 s (`IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR`), the rail monitor pauses that pair, and the slice is retried on another pair. Requests that cannot complete within the 10 s budget fail. The rail monitor state is per worker, so each worker pays the timeout once for the same unreachable pair.

**Measured** (two hosts, five NICs each: `mlx5_0` on the management network, `mlx5_1-4` on four rail subnets with policy routing between them): a 5×5 NIC-pair matrix, each cell an engine restricted to that one pair, agrees with `ib_write_bw` in both directions on all 25 pairs — the 16 rail↔rail pairs work (cross pairs included), `mlx5_0`↔`mlx5_0` works over the management network, and the 8 pairs between `mlx5_0` and a rail NIC do not (`transport retry counter exceeded`, then `Rail paused`). With automatic selection and all five NICs enabled on both sides, the same `test-run` session spent an extra ~18 s (A→B) and ~33 s (B→A) on those pairs before its transfers completed, and a transfer with a 10 s deadline fails outright. On a single host the position-based mapping likewise pairs a rail NIC with the local `mlx5_0`.

**Why it matters**

Default deployments usually leave all NICs enabled; the cost shows up as multi-second stalls and timeouts right after start, and the only trace is a `Rail paused: local_nic=<id> remote_nic=<id>` line after the retry timeout, with NIC indices rather than names. Users work around it with `MC_TE_FILTERS` or a rail file, but only after finding out.

**Possible directions**

When choosing the remote NIC, prefer candidates whose published GID (IPv4-mapped RoCE v2 GIDs carry the subnet) is in the same subnet as, or routable from, the local NIC's address — the descriptor already carries every device's GID; or let the rail file express "no path" pairs; and share an unreachable-pair verdict across workers so the timeout is paid once per pair rather than once per worker. We can prepare a patch if one of these is acceptable.

**Reproduction**

Two hosts with a front-end NIC on a different network than the rail NICs; all NICs enabled; start transfers and watch "Rail paused: local_nic=… remote_nic=…" after ~3.7 s. Our #2864 diagnostics tool shows the matrix with `tent diagnostics test-run --rail-matrix`.

**Environment**: commit `342c8aee`; Linux x86_64 hosts with mlx5 RoCE v2 NICs: a front-end NIC on the management network and four rail NICs on separate subnets with policy routing.

items.title: [Bug]: [Misc] SSD admin CLI tools rebuild full SSH handshake per remote command
items.author: thrower01
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

ontext

Both`python/mooncake/mooncake_ssd_register.py::_execute_ssh_command` and`mooncake_ssd_unregister.py::_execute_ssh_command` open a fresh`paramiko.SSHClient` , run`connect()` , run one command, then call`close()` . No connection reuse.

The register tool calls this function for every SPDK target, and within one target the pattern is:

1. probe`scripts/rpc.py` location (up to 2`test -f` commands)
2. call`nvmf_get_subsystems`
3. for each namespace, call`bdev_get_bdevs`
That is 3 to 5 full SSH handshakes per target — TCP SYN → KEX → userauth → channel open → exec → channel close. Each target pays the handshake multiplier once per discovery run. The unregister tool has the same duplicated code path.

Fix direction

Introduce a process-wide`SSHConnectionPool` in`python/mooncake/_administration.py` keyed by`(ip, port, username, password, key_file)` :

- lazy connect on first`_get_client(key)`
- `get_transport().is_active()` health check before reuse
- single automatic reconnect + retry on`exec_command` failure (handles transient TCP drops)
- `close_all()` /`reset_for_test()` for cleanup
Both admin scripts delegate`_execute_ssh_command()` to the pool. Each SPDK target now shares one SSH handshake across all commands in its discovery flow.

Impact

Reduces per-target handshake count from`O(namespaces + 3)` to`O(1)` ; eliminates repeated KEX CPU work on the remote node; and makes the discovery path resilient to a single transient SSH drop per target. Only affects the two admin CLI tools, which are operator-facing and off the inference / training data path.

Acceptance

- New unit tests covering same-host reuse (1 connect for N commands), cross-host isolation (one connect per distinct host), and reconnect-once after a transient failure.
- Existing`require_paramiko` lazy-import tests keep passing

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA + NEXTN decode graph silently corrupts output on GB10 TP2
items.author: hellojiaru
items.body_excerpt:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues and found no report of this silent semantic-corruption mode.
- [ ] The bug has been revalidated on current SGLang main. The tested image is pinned to the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next day-zero stack described below.
- [x] A public qualification harness and controlled eager/graph comparison are included.
- [x] This report is in English.

## Describe the bug

On 2x GB10 with TP2, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA + NEXTN decode CUDA graphs can return HTTP 200 and substantially higher throughput while silently producing semantically invalid output. We observed two independent failures during the same Graph candidate boot:

1. a 1,024-token non-looping essay test degenerates into repeated punctuation (`!`);
2. an approximately 25K-token prompt containing four ordered markers fails to retrieve the markers and also degenerates into repeated punctuation.

The same model, prompts, and runtime pass both gates with decode CUDA graphs disabled. This is not a timeout, OOM, or server crash. It is silent output corruption and therefore cannot be detected by health checks or throughput benchmarks.

This issue reports only the silent-corruption A/B. It is distinct from #37052, an independent external report of invalid-probability asserts and rank termination. A preceding local overlap-related crash is summarized in the companion repository, but this issue does not claim that the two incidents share one root cause.

## Controlled A/B

Common configuration:

```text
hardware: 2x ASUS Ascent GX10 / NVIDIA GB10 (SM121), TP2 over RoCEv2
model: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4
SGLang base: d91c3682b Qwen3.8-Flash-Next development image plus SM121 QSA/M-RoPE fixes
QSA draft-extend compatibility fix: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37110
dense FP4: flashinfer_cudnn
MoE: flashinfer_cutlass
NEXTN: steps/topk/draft = 3/1/4
Mamba state: float32
linear/GDN backend: triton
max running requests: 2
context: 262144
radix cache: disabled
overlap schedule: disabled
```

Only the graph profile changed:

```text
Eager control:
  --disable-cuda-graph

Graph candidate:
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 2
  --disable-cuda-graph-padding
  --disable-prefill-cuda-graph
  --speculative-attention-mode decode
```

Results:

| Profile | 2,048-token code decode | 1,024-token loop gate | ~25K four-marker retrieval |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Eager | 41.60 / 42.39 / 42.86 tok/s | pass | pass |
| Decode Graph | 50.66 tok/s observed | fail: punctuation repetition | fail: markers missing / punctuation repetition |

The eager control also completed a 16,384-token continuous generation at 48.01 tok/s and then served a short request. Both ranks remained at zero restarts.

## Evidence scope

- The Eager throughput row contains three measurements.
- `50.66 tok/s` is one observed Graph throughput measurement, not a distribution.
- Both semantic failures occurred in one controlled Graph candidate boot. Cross-boot frequency has not yet been measured.
- No OOM, container restart, CUDA assert, or NCCL exit occurred in this semantic-failure run.
- The original result JSON was not preserved as a public artifact. The hardened public harness below is the reproducible gate, not a claim that the historical output has been independently replayed.
- The issue has not been re-run on the latest `qwen4-main-squashed` head or current main.

## Reproduction

The launcher, immutable environment identities, and qualification harness are pinned in companion commit `29198ba1317d1452706a5915f32bbedac919f7b7`:

https://github.com/hellojiaru/qwen38-flash-next-dual-gb10/tree/29198ba1317d1452706a5915f32bbedac919f7b7

The launcher defaults to Eager and guards the rejected Graph profile. Build the pinned image and configure both isolated test nodes as documented in the repository.

Run the Eager control worker-first:

```bash
./start-node.sh start 1 eager
./start-node.sh start 0 eager
python tools/qualify.py --base http://127.0.0.1:8918/v1 --long-tokens 25000 > eager-qualification.json
```

Stop both test ranks, set `ALLOW_REJECTED_PROFILE=1` in `.env` on both isolated nodes, then run the Graph candidate worker-first:

```bash
./start-node.sh start 1 graph-unsafe
./start-node.sh start 0 graph-unsafe
python tools/qualify.py --base http://127.0.0.1:8918/v1 --long-tokens 25000 > graph-qualification.json
```

The harness verifies arithmetic, tool name and JSON arguments, a synthetic vision fixture, reasoning plus the correct final answer, long non-looping output, ordered marker retrieval, and exact bounded responses. It rejects long repeated character/token runs.

The client harness cannot prove process stability. Reproducers should also record both ranks' restart count, `OOMKilled`, scheduler/NCCL errors, and kernel Xid events before and after each profile.

## Expected behavior

Decode CUDA graphs may change performance but must preserve the eager path's token semantics. If the graph path is unsupported for QSA + NEXTN on this stack, startup should fail closed or the graph path should be disabled rather than returning HTTP success with corrupted content.

## Notes

- BF16 Mamba state and a locally enabled FlashInfer GDN path caused separate semantic failures and are not part of this report.
- The companion repository CI is static validation only; it does not run the model or dual-node hardware.
- A current-head reproduction, raw eager/graph JSON outputs, and repeated Graph boots would materially strengthen this report.

items.title: [Bug]  DSV4.1 Flash + DSPARK: CUDA caching allocator exhausts GPU memory under sustained max-batch decode (OOM crash every 15–25 min), KV pool only 29% used
items.author: elain
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSPARK speculative decoding on a single 8×B200 node is **stable under short benchmark windows (< 6 min) but crashes on a fixed ~15–25 minute cadence under sustained max-batch decode load**. Every crash has the same signature: all 8 TP ranks fail a 20 MB `expandable_segments` mapping with only 4–19 MB free, then the engine kills its own process tree. Docker restarts it, and it crashes again ~15–25 min later. Over a 2-hour sustained soak: **6 crashes, identical signature**.

Crucially this is **not a KV-cache capacity problem** — at crash time `full token usage: 0.29, swa token usage: 0.16` (KV pool `max_total_num_tokens=25,826,048`, ~71% of KV headroom unused). The PyTorch caching allocator's non-KV memory grows unboundedly under sustained load.

**Allocator failure — all 8 ranks within the same second (two shown):**

[rank0]:[W1010 01:38:17.257967532 CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:508] expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 0 while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 4718592, total: 191502876672).
[rank4]:[W1010 01:38:17.258494500 CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:508] expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 4 while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 19398656, total: 191502876672).

**Crash handler immediately after:**

[2026-10-10 01:38:23] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=1, include_parent=True, pid=1
[2026-10-10 01:38:24] No live scheduler processes found; skipping py-spy and CUDA coredump.
[2026-10-10 01:38:24] SIGQUIT received. signum=None, frame=None. It usually means one child failed.

**KV pool NOT exhausted at crash time** (last scheduler lines before death):

Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 512, #cached-token: 48896, full token usage: 0.29, swa token usage: 0.16, #running-req: 195, #queue-req: 0

**Mitigation experiments we already ran (both failed, so this looks like unbounded growth, not headroom sizing):**

1. Removing `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` → the server crashes even under trivial load (single-digit concurrent probes) right after startup; the fixed-segment allocator is strictly worse here.
2. Lowering `--mem-fraction-static` 0.75 → 0.73 (frees ~3.8 GB/GPU for the allocator) → **crash cadence unchanged** (4 crashes in 5 sustained windows), same signature.

**Related issues checked and ruled out:**
- #36333 (zombie requests after client disconnect): zero occurrences of `"state was deleted in TokenizerManager"` in our logs.
- #37553 (unbounded `custom_mask` via `torch.cat` in EAGLE/DFlash): DSPARK's verify path passes `custom_mask=None` throughout (`dspark_components/dspark_verify.py`), so it does not use that code path.

Secondary observation: before each crash, sustained throughput degrades ~15–20% vs short-window burst and TTFT/ITL p95 drift up, consistent with growing allocator pressure. This makes the current V4.1 preview unfit for sustained saturated serving on our node (`--restart unless-stopped` recovers in ~8 min per crash as a stopgap). Sustained-load stability may be worth adding to the V4.1 roadmap (#42170) — short-window benchmarks cannot catch this bug class. Happy to provide full container logs / dmesg / workload details on request.

### Reproduction

1. Start the server with the command below.
2. Drive **sustained** saturating decode load at high batch — we replay real SWE agent traces at ~192 concurrent sticky sessions with continuous streaming requests (each request carries its full session prefix, up to ~300K tokens). Any sustained max-batch decode workload with DSPARK on should work.
3. Within 15–25 minutes the process dies with the allocator signature above; docker restarts it; it dies again every 15–25 min.
4. Note: 6-minute benchmark windows never trigger it — the failure only appears under sustained load, so a quick `bench_serving` pass will look clean.

Launch command:

```bash
docker run -d --name sglang_standalone --network host --ipc host --gpus all \
  --shm-size 67108864 --restart unless-stopped \
  -v /data/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/models:ro \
  -e SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=60 -e PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
  lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tp 8 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --trust-remote-code \
  --context-length 1048576 --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 256 --enable-cache-report --enable-metrics \
  --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --log-level info

Startup reference numbers: max_total_num_tokens=25826048, available_gpu_mem≈20.5 GB after init.

### Environment

```markdown
- Hardware: 8 × NVIDIA B200 (192 GB each, SM100), single node, NVLink, host network
- Driver / CUDA: 580.178.04 / CUDA 13.0.3 (in container); torch 2.13.0+cu130; NCCL 2.30.7
- SGLang: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41@sha256:4a5d132a06a7` (sglang 0.0.0.dev1+gda64c5cbb) — this is still the newest V4.1 preview digest as of 2026-10-10
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (476 GB, bundled 3-stage DSPARK draft, `num_nextn_predict_layers=3`)
- Workload: SWE agent-trace session replay — 400 sticky sessions replayed continuously, ~192 concurrent sessions, streaming (`stream=true`, `include_usage`), per-request prompts carry full session history (up to ~300K tokens)
- Quant/KV defaults: KV dtype fp8_e4m3, attention backend dsv

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (dsv4 + DSPARK): multi-turn prefix cache degrades to a constant ~11.5K-token hit — 60–80K conversation prefix re-prefilled every turn (GLM-5.3-Flash unaffected in the same   environment)
items.author: F0rtiter
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (dsv4 / FlashMLA hybrid KV pool, DSPARK speculative decoding) for
  Claude Code traffic (Anthropic `/v1/messages` via a relay). Prefix reuse works correctly at the
  beginning of the run; after the server has been up for a while, **every turn of a long agentic
  session hits exactly 11,520 cached tokens and re-prefills the whole 60–80K-token conversation
  prefix**, and the state persists.

  Log excerpt — consecutive turns ~10 s apart (TP0, default `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`;
  `#cached-token: 0` on chunks 2..N of the *same* request is expected for chunked prefill — the
  problem is that the first chunk's hit never grows across turns):

  ```
  [21:51:38] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 4096, #cached-token: 11520, full token usage: 0.00, swa token usage: 0.00, ... #pending-token: 60864
  [21:51:38–45]  15 more chunks of the same turn, all #cached-token: 0, #pending-token: 60864 → 0
                 → turn total ≈ 76,480 prompt tokens, 64,960 recomputed
  [21:51:46] Prefill batch, #new-token: 4096, #cached-token: 11520, #pending-token: 62293   → turn ≈ 77,909 tokens (+~1.4K vs previous turn)
  [21:51:55] Prefill batch, #new-token: 4096, #cached-token: 11520, #pending-token: 66335   → turn ≈ 81,951
  [21:52:06] Prefill batch, #new-token: 4096, #cached-token: 11520, #pending-token: 67712   → turn ≈ 83,328
  ```

  Expected: turn N+1 is a strict append of turn N, so it should hit ≈ turn N's full prompt and
  prefill only the appended ~1–4K tokens. Observed: hit pinned at exactly 11520 (45 × 256-token
  pages — consistent with the stable system prompt), everything after it recomputed.

Key observations:

  - **GLM-5.3-Flash control:** with the *same* host, relay, and Claude Code client, GLM-5.3-Flash
    shows normal multi-turn prefix hits on comparable traffic. Only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash degrades.
    This argues against the client-side causes documented in #35129 (`cch=` request mutation,
    task-list snapshot churn), since those would corrupt prefixes for any model behind the same
    relay.
  - `full token usage: 0.00` / `swa token usage: 0.00` while `#full token` ≈ 76–82K → the device
    pool is nowhere near full; plain capacity eviction should not produce a *stable* miss boundary.
  - The hit length is byte-stable at 11520 across turns → the effective divergence point sits right
    after the system prompt.
  - DSPARK speculative decoding is active (decode logs show `accept len` 3.4–4.8).
  - Earlier in the run, multi-turn hits were normal.

  Relation to #35129: same family (DSv4 + Flash + Claude Code agentic sessions; long multi-chunk
  requests lose prefix reuse). Of the three causes #35129 closed with, HiCache load-back eviction
  storms are ruled out by configuration here (no `--enable-hierarchical-cache`;
  `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1` only offloads the engram *embedding* hash table to host
  memory, not the KV path), and the two client-side causes are made unlikely by the GLM control
  above.

Suspected area (not yet verified — the dsv4.1-specific cache structures that GLM-5.3-Flash does
  not share):

  - the DSv4 compressed indexer sidecars (c4 / c128 pools, `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`,
    `index_key_cache.py`, `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py`) — if a bounded auxiliary structure stops
    accepting or exposing entries once full, matches would get capped at a stable boundary exactly
    like this, while `full token usage` stays ~0;
  - SWA-tombstone match validation in the unified tree (`unified_cache/components/swa.py`);
  - radix-cache insertion on the DSPARK verify path (`speculative/dspark_components/`).

  Diagnostics (happy to post results):

  1. **Identical-body replay:** send the same >64K-token request twice back-to-back and compare
     `#cached-token` — distinguishes engine-side (second request still only hits 11520) from
     request-content drift.
  2. A/B with `--speculative-algorithm` removed, same traffic.
  3. Watch `evicted_tokens_total` / pool usage on `/metrics` across the degradation moment.

### Reproduction

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `--attention-backend dsv4` (`page_size=256` auto-forced), TP=8 / EP=1,
    `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, default `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`.
  - Workload: Claude Code sessions over `/v1/messages`; turn N+1 = turn N + appended messages;
    prompts grow 76K → 83K tokens. Degradation appears after the server has been running for a
    while and then persists.
  - Minimal form: any two consecutive append-only requests whose prompt spans several
    chunked-prefill chunks (~64K+ tokens here) sent seconds apart; in the degraded state every turn
    logs `#cached-token: 11520`.

  Launch command (Docker, image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev`):

 ```
  sglang serve \
    --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
    --tp 8 --ep-size 1 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
    --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
    --attention-backend dsv4 \
    --moe-runner-backend marlin \
    --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
    --max-running-requests 64 \
    --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
    --served-model-name reasoner \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --swa-prefix-tails 1024 \
    --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report \
    --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
    --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
    --watchdog-timeout 3600

  # container env (not KV-cache related, listed for completeness):
  #   SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=

items.title: fp16 and bf16 constants are rounded twice through fp32, 1 ulp off near ties
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

fp16 and bf16 constants are rounded twice: from the Python float (a double) to fp32, and then to the 16-bit type. A value just above a 16-bit rounding tie loses the bits that break the tie, and the tie then rounds to even, 1 ulp too low.

```python
import numpy as np
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(X, Z, V: tl.constexpr, N: tl.constexpr):
    offs = tl.arange(0, N)
    tl.store(Z + offs, tl.full([N], V, tl.float16))
    tl.store(Z + N + offs, tl.load(X + offs) * V)


v = 1 + 2**-11 + 2**-30  # just above the fp16 tie between 0x3C00 and 0x3C01
z = torch.empty(32, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda")
kernel[(1, )](torch.ones(16, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda"), z, V=v, N=16)
print(hex(z.view(torch.uint16)[0].item()), hex(z.view(torch.uint16)[16].item()))
print(hex(np.array([v], np.float16).view(np.uint16)[0]))
```

```
0x3c00 0x3c00
0x3c01
```

Expected `0x3c01` (what numpy gives) for both `tl.full` and the multiplication. bf16 has the same problem, e.g. `1 + 2**-8 + 2**-30` gives `0x3f80` instead of `0x3f81`.

`get_fp16` and `get_bf16` in `python/src/ir.cc` take a C++ `float`, so pybind rounds the double to fp32 before it is converted to the 16-bit type. In the interpreter, `get_bf16` also goes through fp32 (`get_fp16` uses numpy and is correct).

The error is at most 1 ulp, and only for values within an fp32 ulp of a 16-bit tie.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8

items.title: `tl.dot` with `input_precision="bf16x3"` or `"bf16x6"` and K=8 returns twice the product
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`tl.dot` on fp32 operands with `input_precision="bf16x3"` or `"bf16x6"` and K=8 returns exactly twice the product. K=8 is accepted for fp32 operands, and `ieee`, `tf32` and `tf32x3` give the right result at K=8.

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(A, B, C, K: tl.constexpr, PRECISION: tl.constexpr):
    m = tl.arange(0, 16)
    k = tl.arange(0, K)
    a = tl.load(A + m[:, None] * K + k[None, :])
    b = tl.load(B + k[:, None] * 16 + m[None, :])
    tl.store(C + m[:, None] * 16 + m[None, :], tl.dot(a, b, input_precision=PRECISION))


for precision in ["ieee", "tf32", "tf32x3", "bf16x3", "bf16x6"]:
    for K in (8, 16):
        a = torch.ones(16, K, device="cuda")
        b = torch.ones(K, 16, device="cuda")
        c = torch.empty(16, 16, device="cuda")
        kernel[(1, )](a, b, c, K, precision)
        print(f"{precision:7} K={K:2}: expected {K}, got {c[0, 0].item()}")
```

```
ieee    K= 8: expected 8, got 8.0
ieee    K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
tf32    K= 8: expected 8, got 8.0
tf32    K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
tf32x3  K= 8: expected 8, got 8.0
tf32x3  K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
bf16x3  K= 8: expected 8, got 16.0
bf16x3  K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
bf16x6  K= 8: expected 8, got 16.0
bf16x6  K=16: expected 16, got 16.0
```

The frontend allows K >= 8 for 32-bit operands (`min_dot_size` in `third_party/nvidia/backend/compiler.py`). `F32DotTC` then splits the fp32 dot into bf16 dots with the same K=8, below the K >= 16 that the frontend requires for 16-bit operands. `AccelerateMatmul` relies on that requirement when it picks the MMAv2 operand layout (the comment above the `minBitwidth` computation in `BlockedToMMA` says it assumes K >= 256 / bitwidth), so the bf16 dots with K=8 are lowered as if K were 16. All values are doubled, for every shape and `num_warps` I tried, including batched (3-D) dots.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8

items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-1010-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 12.0.140 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0-7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (single GPU used for this report, TP=1) Nvidia driver version : 580.173.02 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8481C CPU @ 2.70GHz CPU(s): 208 Hypervisor vendor: KVM ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.28.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: NV18 all-to-all (8x H100 SXM), TP=1 used Relevant packages: vllm==0.28.0 torch==2.13.0 transformers==5.15.1 flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 compressed-tensors==0.17.0 xgrammar==0.2.3 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary.** `--enable-prefix-caching` together with MTP speculative decoding still corrupts output on hybrid (GDN/Mamba) Qwen3.5-class models in **v0.28.0**. A small fraction of responses degenerate into repeated punctuation (`!!!!…`) or come back empty. This is the same failure as #43559, which was closed as completed on 2026-08-06 — the merged scheduler-side fix (#51113) does not cover it, and the cache-manager-side fixes (#43650, #48375) are still open. **Model.** Qwen3.5-architecture dense 27B VLM (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers + full attention every 4th layer, vision tower), FP8 W8A8 compressed-tensors (`FP8_DYNAMIC`), with an MTP head present in the checkpoint (`Qwen3_5MTP` resolves at startup). TP=1, single H100. **Server command** (paths redacted): ```bash export VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm serve \ --served-model-name path-mini \ --port 8000 \ --max-model-len 62768 \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 10 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' ``` Startup confirms the configuration: `Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP`, `enable_prefix_caching=True`, `num_spec_tokens=2`, `GPU KV cache size: 576,637 tokens`, attention block size 800 (forced up to match the mamba page size), async scheduling enabled (default). **Workload.** Multi-step GUI-agent traces: each request is a conversation of prior steps plus 1–3 screenshots (sliding 2-image history), ~4k–12k prompt tokens, ~20–100 output tokens, `temperature=0`, client concurrency up to 32. Consecutive steps of the same episode share a long prefix, so prefix-cache hit rate climbs through a run. **Observed.** | vLLM | prefix caching | MTP | final prefix-cache hit rate | malformed responses | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0.26.0 | on | k=2 | 27.5% | 25 / 2,636 (0.95%) | | **0.28.0** | **on** | **k=2** | **31.7%** | **4 / 495 (0.81%)** | | 0.28.0 | on | k=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | ~10% (see note) | 0 / 1,135 | Malformed = response is a run of repeated `!` characters, or empty content. `finish_reason` is normal; no HTTP 5xx, no crash, no traceback — the engine stays healthy and every other response in the same run is correct. Two observations that point at the prefix cache rather than at MTP alone: 1. **Rate tracks cache hit rate.** Corruption appears only once the prefix cache starts hitting, and scales with the hit rate. 2. **`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` appears to avoid it, but only by destroying the cache.** With fp8 KV, vLLM raises the attention block size 800 → 1600 (`platforms/interface.py`, so that one attention page covers one mamba page). Our requests share ~1,700 tokens of prefix, so at a 1600-token matching unit almost nothing is reusable: hit rate collapses from 31.7% to ~10%, and malformed responses go to 0/1,135. That is consistent with reduced exposure, not with fp8 fixing the underlying defect. (For the same reason `--block-size 800` cannot be used to compensate: the value is derived and only ever raised.) **Suspected cause** (already described in #43650 / #48375): `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` in `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` accepts `drop_eagle_block` and never acts on it, so the final matched block — which can hold recurrent state written over draft positions that verification later rejected — stays reachable through the prefix cache and is reused by subsequent requests sharing that prefix. `FullAttentionManager` drops that block. In v0.28.0 the caller (`kv_cache_coordinator.py`) additionally skips the eagle margin for `MambaSpec` with the comment *"its finder never drops"*, i.e. caller and manager disagree about who is responsible. Applying **#43650** (6 lines, `max_num_blocks -= 1` when `use_eagle`) on top of v0.28.0 starts cleanly and shows no regression on an unrelated accuracy check (100 grounding requests at concurrency 32: 76% vs 75% unpatched, identical coor

items.title: [Bug]: Speculative decoding (mtp and dflash) silently disables prefix-cache hits for hybrid GDN models on nightly; worked on v0.24.0
items.author: cgoudie
items.body_excerpt:
(analysis by Fable 5)
### Your current environment

- DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121`/`sm_121a`, aarch64, 128 GB unified memory), Docker `--network host --gpus all --ipc host`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` → reports `v0.28.1rc1.dev43+g6f7df92a8`
- Comparison baseline on the same host: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0`
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (hybrid GDN: 48 linear-attention + 16 full-attention layers, built-in MTP head). Also reproduced with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` + `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (rev `dedf8df`).
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 65536`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.30`, env `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On the current nightly, enabling **any** speculative decoding method (built-in `mtp` or `dflash`) on a hybrid GDN model silently drops `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` to **0** — align-mode prefix caching engages at startup (log: `Mamba cache mode is set to 'align' for Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) but never hits, and repeated long prompts pay full re-prefill. The identical command minus `--speculative-config` hits normally. No crash, no warning — the caching is just inert, so this is easy to miss in production.

A/B on the same host, same model, same 18,219-token prompt sent twice (`max_tokens=10`):

| nightly config | TTFT req1 → req2 | `prefix_cache_hits_total` delta |
|---|---|---|
| APC only (no spec) | 9.46 s → **0.64 s** | **17,248** |
| APC + `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` | 23.6 s → 13.9 s* | **0** |
| APC + `{"method":"dflash", ..., "num_speculative_tokens":7}` | 12.9 s → 12.5 s | **0** |

\* the MTP row also shows a large decode regression on this platform (10.5 tok/s vs 19.7 on v0.24.0 with the same flags — possibly a separate sm_121 issue; noting it for context, not the subject of this report).

**On `v0.24.0`, MTP + align-mode APC coexist correctly** on the same host/model: repeated 9,901-token prompt → 8,000 tokens hit, TTFT 7.27 s → 1.33 s, with `mtp` k=3 active. So spec+APC coexistence for hybrids existed and regressed somewhere between v0.24.0 and the current nightly.

Repro (nightly):

```bash
docker run --rm --init --network host --gpus all --ipc host \
  -v /opt/models:/models -e CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a \
  vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /models/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4 \
  --served-model-name bench --port 10099 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# send any >3,300-token prompt twice; watch vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total stay 0
# drop --speculative-config and the second send hits ~all full blocks
```

Possibly related but distinct: #53670 (hits occur but recompute per hit), #41884 (DFlash+APC IndexError crash — we see silent zero-hit, not a crash), #26201 (tracking).

Is the suppression intentional (spec-decode + hybrid APC support not yet wired on the new path), or a regression? If intentional, a startup warning like the align-mode one would save users from silently losing their cache. Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware.

items.title: Feature Request: Graceful reasoning budget termination. Avoid mid-sentence cutoff.
items.author: CleStil
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

PR #20297 (merged ~2025-03-11) added `--reasoning-budget-message`, which injects
a string at the hard token cutoff to signal the model to wrap up. The injection
still happens at exactly token N with zero warning. The model gets no time to
finish its current thought before the `</think>` boundary.

Graceful termination before the cutoff is expected to improve reasoning
performance. See Motivation and Possible Implementation for details.


### Motivation

Raw truncation of the thinking trace measurably reduces answer quality compared
to graceful termination. Muennighoff et al. (s1: Simple test-time scaling,
arXiv:2501.19393) showed that appending an end-of-thinking delimiter with
"Final Answer:" before the hard cut outperforms naïve truncation. This was
confirmed by follow-up work (arXiv:2505.05315), which states directly that
"the S1 approach performs better than directly truncating the full reasoning
trajectory, underscoring the importance of preserving the solution segment."

The current --reasoning-budget-message implementation injects a wrap-up message
at exactly token N, leaving the model zero tokens to actually act on it. This is
functionally equivalent to truncation with a cosmetic suffix — the model cannot
produce a meaningful conclusion within 0 remaining tokens.

### Possible Implementation

Three approaches in increasing complexity:

Option A — message offset
Inject the budget message at `budget - offset` instead of `budget`, giving the
model `offset` tokens to act on the wrap-up signal. The s1 paper
(https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393) shows this outperforms raw truncation.
Change in the COUNTING state of reasoning-budget.cpp:

    if (ctx->remaining <= ctx->warn_offset)  // was: <= 0

Files: reasoning-budget.cpp, reasoning-budget.h, common.h, arg.cpp,
sampling.cpp. Default 0 preserves current behavior.

Option B — separate budgeting
Split total budget into thinking (t) and conclusion (s) phases, t + s = budget.
Force `</think>` at token t, leave s tokens for a conclusion before the answer.
Follow-up work on s1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05315) shows this outperforms
the basic offset approach. Would add a second parameter, e.g.
--reasoning-budget-conclusion M.

Option C — logit biasing toward `</think>`
Ramp up the logit weight of `</think>` as the budget runs low, then force it at
the hard limit. No dependency on an injected phrase, model-agnostic. NVIDIA NIM
uses this approach with a 10% extension window for sentence completion. More
invasive (sampler changes) but cleanest long-term.

Options A and B build on the existing message injection architecture. Option C
is a parallel approach that could coexist with either.

Happy to test on ROCm/gfx1100 (Qwen3.5-27B) and contribute a draft of Option A
or B if there is interest.

items.title: server: hybrid-model slot livelocks on "erasing old context checkpoint" at the same position (qwen4exp, Vulkan, b10731)
items.author: TamasZagyi
items.body_excerpt:
# server: hybrid-model slot livelocks on "erasing old context checkpoint" at the same position (qwen4exp, Vulkan)

## Summary

On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`qwen4exp`, 36 gated-delta-net + 12 attention layers) served by
`llama-server` with two slots and the server prompt cache, a slot occasionally stops
advancing during prompt processing and loops forever on context-checkpoint creation at
one position. The request never completes, the process burns one core, and because the
slot never frees, the whole server (and llama-swap in front of it) is stuck: a request
for another model waited 4 minutes and got nothing. Freeing the slot needs an unload of
the model.

Reproduced twice in one night on two different quants and two different load modes,
and once the day before, so it is neither the quant nor the engram placement.

## Environment

- llama.cpp **b10731**, `llama-b10731-bin-win-vulkan-x64` (0.3.0-dev, commit 0eadefeb), Windows 11
- AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), Vulkan, AMD proprietary driver, 128 GB unified (96 GB carve)
- Model: unsloth `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-IQ4_XS (also seen on UD-Q2_K_XL)
- Command (the IQ4_XS case):

```
llama-server --port 10005 -ngl 99 -fa on -lm mmap -b 2048 -ub 512 --poll 100
  -m Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf
  --lazy-mode on -c 131072 -np 2 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0 --jinja
```

(the Q2_K_XL case was `-lm dio --lazy-mode off -ot "per_layer_token_embd=CPU" -c 262144 -np 2`, otherwise identical)

## What happens

The client is a voice assistant that pins one conversation to slot 0 (`id_slot: 0`) and
sends a ~11K-token prompt that is almost entirely a prefix of the previous request
(cache_prompt on). Most turns take 5-10 s. Roughly one turn in ten never returns. The
client gave up after 240 s; llama-server kept the slot busy afterwards.

`GET /slots` while it was stuck (13 minutes after the client disconnected):

```
{"id":0,"n_ctx":65536,"speculative":false,"is_processing":true,"id_task":9440,
 "n_prompt_tokens":11128,"n_prompt_tokens_processed":167,"n_prompt_tokens_cache":0,
 "params":{"seed":4294967295,"temperature":0.0, ... "top_k":20,"top_p":0.95,"min_p":0.0, ...
```

Server log, the same two lines repeating every ~600 ms for the whole 13 minutes:

```
W slot create_check: id  0 | task 9440 | erasing old context checkpoint (pos_min = 11127, pos_max = 11127, n_tokens = 11128, size = 112.571 MiB)
W slot create_check: id  0 | task 9440 | erasing old context checkpoint (pos_min = 11127, pos_max = 11127, n_tokens = 11128, size = 112.571 MiB)
```

Note `n_prompt_tokens_processed` stays at 167 while the checkpoint is created and erased
at `pos_min == pos_max == n_tokens - 1`. The other slot keeps serving normally. `POST
/api/models/unload/<model>` on llama-swap (i.e. killing the process) is the only thing
that freed it; no `--slot-save-path` was configured.

## Expected

The slot finishes prompt processing (or fails the task) instead of looping on
checkpoint creation at one position.

## Notes

- Seen on b10731 with both `-lm dio --lazy-mode off -ot per_layer_token_embd=CPU` and
  `-lm mmap --lazy-mode on`, UD-Q2_K_XL and UD-IQ4_XS, `-c 262144` and `-c 131072`, always
  `-np 2`, always on the pinned slot 0 with a large cached prefix, temperature 0.0 in
  the stuck request.
- Full slot JSON and the repeating log excerpt follow (captured the night it was caught).

- Possibly related: #22384 / #28194 (context checkpoints on hybrid/recurrent models).

items.title: [Proposal] reasoning budget: soft end-token wind-down instead of hard FORCING at the wall (+ sm_70 notes)
items.author: NightPoetry
items.body_excerpt:
# [Discussion/Feature] Volta (sm_70) notes: spark2_5 on 16GB V100, DRY/reasoning-budget behavior, and a proposal: soft wind-down ramp for the reasoning budget

## Setup

- Tesla V100 16GB (sm_70), CUDA 12.6, self-built master (commit 8172e65 era, + sm_70 arch), `GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON`
- Model: spark2_5 (iFlytek Spark-X2.5-4B, Q8_0, ~4GB), served via llama-server
- All numbers below are single-run measurements on this card

## 1. spark2_5 runs well on Volta — 512K context on 16GB

- `-c 524288 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0 -fa on` loads and serves fine in ~15.8GB VRAM (mixed KV quant: q8_0 for K, q5_0 for V)
- prefill ~2770 t/s, decode ~96 t/s at ~2.9K-token prompts (llama-cli timings)
- At 512K the KV cache fills the card, so the server runs with a single slot; there is no VRAM left for a second concurrent request.

## 2. Repetition loops: DRY fixes them (data)

A repetition-inducing pair of tasks (30-item list + 800-word story), character 12-gram repeat rate:

| config | merged repeat rate | worst single-gram dup |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (temp 0.6 / top_k 20 / rep_penalty 1.0) | 0.271 | **41** (hard loop) |
| + DRY (`--dry-penalty-last-n 1024 --dry-multiplier 0.8 --dry-base 1.75`) | 0.085 | 2 |
| + DRY + `--reasoning-budget 4096` | **0.039** | 3 |

DRY fully broke the loop. Confirmed: `--dry-penalty-last-n` defaults to 0 (disabled) — it must be set explicitly.

## 3. Over-thinking: budget behavior (and a proposal)

With a small budget, the current sampler hard-forces the message + end tag at the wall (the FORCING state sets all other logits to -inf). Works, and the configurable `--reasoning-budget-message` makes it graceful.

**Proposal: a soft wind-down ramp.** Instead of entering FORCING at the wall, bias the logits of the end sequence's first token progressively as the budget is consumed, and let the remaining counter go negative — the ramp keeps intensifying until the model closes the reasoning block on its own. FORCING stays in the code as a backstop path but is no longer entered at zero:

```cpp
// apply(), COUNTING state
const int32_t ramp = std::max(ctx->budget / 4, 32);
if (ctx->remaining <= ramp) {
    const float t   = 1.0f - (float) ctx->remaining / (float) ramp;   // keeps growing past 1
    const float bias = 8.0f * t * t;
    for (const auto & seq : ctx->end_matcher.seqs)
        if (!seq.empty() && (size_t) seq[0] < cur_p->size)
            cur_p->data[seq[0]].logit += bias;
}
```

The same patch also handles the empty-answer failure mode: once the reasoning block closes, EOS is suppressed for the next 64 tokens, so a capped-budget run still writes the answer body instead of stopping with an empty answer.

**Observed with this patch** (budget 4096, thinking on, three runs of the same over-thinking-prone prompt):

| run | what happened |
|---|---|
| 1 | thinking hit the client `max_tokens` cap before reaching the budget (the model would have kept going) |
| 2 | model closed the reasoning on its own at 1470 tokens, well before the wall |
| 3 | thinking stopped right at the budget line (~4096 tokens), then a complete, correct answer followed — the hard-injected budget message never appeared in the output |

For contrast, the same prompt at budget 4000 without the patch: still digit-by-digit converting at the wall, no answer.

## 4. Question

Would a soft wind-down ramp (biased end-token probability near the wall, FORCING kept as backstop) be acceptable upstream — as a flag (e.g. `--reasoning-budget-soft`) or as the default behavior? The change is one file (`common/reasoning-budget.cpp`), about 40 lines.

FWIW on the same card: `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ=ON` measured +3.5% prefill / +0.7% gen at a ~2.9K-token prompt (single run, within noise) — kept ON per the build docs' Volta note. The patch, benchmark
numbers and a README live in [NightPoetry/llama.cpp-soft-reasoning-budget](https://github.com/NightPoetry/llama.cpp-soft-reasoning-budget), and the branch
[`reasoning-budget-soft-ramp`](https://github.com/NightPoetry/llama.cpp/tree/reasoning-budget-soft-ramp) is ready if a PR is useful. Feedback on the design
(ramp shape, thresholds, whether the anti-empty window belongs here) is welcome.

items.title: [RFC]: [Store] Add object storage as a first-class replica tier
items.author: particle128
items.body_excerpt:
### Changes proposed # [RFC]: [Store] Add object storage as a first-class replica tier This proposal introduces object storage as a first-class replica tier, reusing the [existing OSS adapter](https://kvcache-ai.github.io/Mooncake/design/store/oss-backend.html). The new types, configuration options, and protocol extensions below are proposed changes. ## 1. Goals and scope The current object storage integration follows the FileStorage / LOCAL_DISK path: the MEMORY owner performs uploads, and reads also depend on that owner. This proposal introduces an `OBJECT_STORAGE` replica alongside MEMORY, LOCAL_DISK, DFS, and NOF_SSD: - The Master manages object locations, replica states, and lifecycle; Clients access shared object storage directly using descriptors. - The Master configures one of three write modes: synchronous writes, asynchronous replication after a memory write, or direct offload on memory eviction. - Object replicas support deletion and background reclamation. - Once an object replica is committed, other Clients can read it even after the original writer/owner goes offline. The initial implementation reuses the OSS adapter while keeping the interface provider-neutral. Each Mooncake object maps to one backend object. Object aggregation, cascading MEMORY → SSD → object storage, a unified redesign of all external storage tiers, and general idempotency enhancements to the shared Start/End/Revoke protocol are out of scope. ## 2. Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph MP["Master process"] M["Object directory, write mode, lease / pin"] M --> D["Existing MEMORY / LOCAL_DISK / DFS / NOF_SSD"] M --> O["New OBJECT_STORAGE
object_key + object_size"] M --> G["Pending deletions / retries
Existing background maintenance"] G -->|"DELETE after protection ends"| GA["ObjectStorageAdapter
Master-side instance"] end C["Requesting Client / SDK"] <-->|"PutStart / PutEnd / Query"| M C -->|"Synchronous writes / direct reads"| B["ObjectStorageBackend"] W["MEMORY owner
Offload executor"] -. "Fetch tasks / report completion" .-> M W -->|"Background upload from MEMORY"| B B --> A["ObjectStorageAdapter
Client-side GetBatch / PutBatch"] A --> S["Shared object storage"] GA --> S classDef added fill:#fff0d6,stroke:#d97706,stroke-width:2px; class O,B,G added; ``` - Backends and adapters are in-process modules, with separate instances in each participating process. The Master does not carry object GET/PUT data traffic, but uses its own adapter for background DELETE operations. - Deletion and retries reuse the Master's existing background maintenance mechanism, without requiring a dedicated GC thread or service. Only known pending deletions are processed; the entire bucket is not scanned. - Both background modes reuse the owner's offload queue, heartbeat, and source-replica protection, extending them with an object-storage target and completion reporting. Reads no longer depend on the owner after the object replica is committed. - As with DFS, the Master manages replicas while Clients access shared storage directly. Objects are addressed by key, without file-offset allocation or inheritance from the DFS allocator interface. ## 3. Metadata and configuration ### 3.1 Replica descriptor ```cpp struct ObjectStorageDescriptor { std::string object_key; uint64_t object_size; }; // Added to ReplicateConfig size_t os_replica_num{0}; ``` `ObjectStorageDescriptor` is added to the existing `Replica::Descriptor::descriptor_variant`. Replica `id` and `status` remain in the shared outer descriptor rather than being duplicated in the object descriptor. Enabling object replicas requires support in the Master and all participating Clients. The initial implementation does not promise mixed-version operation with older releases. - `os_replica_num` initially supports 0 or 1, defaulting to 0. A value of 1 requests one object replica according to the Master's policy. It is neither the object service's internal replication factor nor an indication that the replica is already complete. - The initial write requires at least one MEMORY replica. After the object replica is committed, MEMORY replicas may be evicted under the normal protection rules. - `object_key` is a backend object name allocated by the Master, separate from the application's key. The adapter handles prefixes and encoding. - Upsert, Put after Remove, and reallocation after abandoning an old task use new object names, so late uploads or old deletion tasks cannot affect new data. Ordinary retries of the same task reuse its `object_key`. This does not introduce a user-facing multi-version KV API. - Existing shared object-checksum metadata is reused; provider ETags are not treated as a generic content checksum. Using a separate object name isolates successive values of the same application key. For example, if `Put(K)` follows `Remove(K)` before the old background DELETE finishes, using K for both backend objects would let the delayed DELETE remove the new data. The Master maps the application key to an `object_key`, so old tasks operate only on the old object. The same isolation applies to Upsert and late uploads. ### 3.2 Cluster-wide backend configuration Initially, each cluster uses a single object storage backend. The Master publishes non-secret configuration to Clients: provider, endpoint, bucket/namespace, and prefix. Clients fetch and cache it during initialization. The Master uses the same storage target for reclamation; descriptors do not duplicate this configuration. An object's full location is **the cluster-wide endpoint / bucket / prefix plus `object_key`**. Client-side and Master-side adapters use credentials configured in their respective processes, reusing the existing OSS environment variables without introducing a credential service: ```text MOONCAKE_OSS_ACCESS_KEY_ID MOONCAKE_OSS_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET MOONCAKE_OSS_SECURITY_TOK

items.title: [RFC] Model-independent Engram byte tables with owned local storage and CUDA stream lookup
items.author: magicYang1573
items.body_excerpt:
## Motivation
The existing layer/head Engram API works for DeepSeek-shaped tables. SGLang also needs N-gram and per-layer input tables with different packing, scaling and sharding. This proposes one additional table-oriented mode on `EngramStore`, with no new public spec or request-handle classes.

## Proposed contract
- `EngramStore(tables={name: {num_rows, row_bytes}}, namespace=..., local_dir=... | store_client=...)`.
- `populate(table_id, rows)` copies immutable CPU byte rows into Store-owned storage.
- `lookup(table_ids, ids, output, *, offsets=None, stream=None)` reads int32/int64 `[T,K]` IDs into uint8 `[T,K,R]`. Repeated table names and nonoverlapping token-major/head-major output are supported. ID -1 preserves output; offsets convert global IDs into table-local rows.
- CPU lookup is synchronous. Local CUDA lookup enqueues complete work on the supplied stream and returns None. Consumers use ordinary streams/events. Warmup before CUDA graph capture and Store/tensor lifetime requirements are explicit.
- `get_table_spec`, `remove`, `close`; the existing layer constructor and methods remain available.

## Local implementation
A Python facade owns namespaced immutable mmap snapshots, validates layouts and performs atomic create-only publication. A private pybind/CUDA helper registers host pages and gathers byte rows directly into CUDA output. It does not depend on PyTorch headers or implement model math. This first version pins selected tables in full; it is not a host page cache.

## Scope and relationship to existing work
This revisits the owned-local idea in #4083 with a model-independent interface and compatibility for the upstream layer API. It does not include the remote gather optimization in #4502 or the experimental feat/engram-pipelined-read transport. Store-backed CPU reads continue through existing ranged reads; remote CUDA/pipeline work remains separate.

A companion SGLang change keeps adapters under mem_cache/engram and changes only table construction/lookup entry points for DeepSeek V4.1, Qwen4-Exp, LongCat Ngram, and Gemma3n/Gemma4. Hashes, scales, projections, request history and collectives remain in SGLang.

## Validation
Local API tests currently pass for CPU layouts, persistence/reopen, validation, CUDA stream ordering and graph replay with changing IDs. Adapter tests pass for BF16, FP8 with table scaling and FP8/E8M0 block scaling. Real-checkpoint local end-to-end comparisons and packaging validation are in progress; their results will be reported in the PR rather than inferred from these unit tests.

## Review points
- Is the table API appropriately scoped for upstream while retaining the existing layer API?
- Is a Python facade plus private CUDA helper acceptable for the first local implementation?
- Immutable snapshot semantics, full-table pinning and graph lifetime requirements should be settled before broader consumers adopt the API.

AI assistance: implementation and this RFC were prepared with Codex; human review is pending.

items.title: `nll_loss2d` (spatial `cross_entropy`) on CUDA: fp16 `mean` reduction returns inf/NaN and all-zero gradients once total weight exceeds fp16 range
items.author: vickiiimu
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

With fp16 inputs outside autocast, `nll_loss` with `reduction="mean"` returns inf once the sum of the loss passes 65,504, and (with typical loss values) NaN once the `total_weight` passes 65,504. Once `total_weight` overflows, the gradient silently zeros. This behavior occurs even when the true answer fits within fp16.

Repro code was written by Claude Opus 5.5, but underwent human review.
```python
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
torch.manual_seed(0)
C = 21
for H in (128, 181, 256):
    x = torch.randn(1, C, H, H, device="cuda", dtype=torch.half, requires_grad=True)
    y = torch.randint(0, C, (1, H, H), device="cuda")
    loss = F.cross_entropy(x, y)
    loss.backward()
    ref = F.cross_entropy(x.detach().double(), y).item()
    print(f"{H*H} px: loss {loss.item()} (fp64 {ref:.4f}), "
          f"all-zero grad: {bool((x.grad == 0).all())}")
```

Output from the code:
```
16384 px: loss 3.513671875 (fp64 3.5139), all-zero grad: False
32761 px: loss inf (fp64 3.4996), all-zero grad: False
65536 px: loss nan (fp64 3.5051), all-zero grad: True
```

This is happening because each block’s fp32 partial sum is cast to fp16 and then added into an fp16 global accumulator through the gpuAtomicAdd step. 
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/8a4e3bc71cc6c15443fa3d74a54cf63f767b9a26/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/NLLLoss2d.cu#L124-L125 

Both `output` and `total_weight` are allocated with the input's dtype. 
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/8a4e3bc71cc6c15443fa3d74a54cf63f767b9a26/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/NLLLoss2d.cu#L502-L503 

The sum overflows first (becomes inf) then the count overflows as well (and inf/inf = NaN). The backward divides by `total_weight`, https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/8a4e3bc71cc6c15443fa3d74a54cf63f767b9a26/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/NLLLoss2d.cu#L182-L183 
which results in zero gradients once `total_weight` is inf.

Autocast is unaffected because autocast calculates nll_loss in fp32. Got the same results on 2.14.1 and nightly 2.16.0.dev20261015 on an L40S.

I’d like to work on a fix for this, and since the cross block accumulation is also why the op is non-deterministic (#17350), it might make sense to address these together. #197565 identifies an fp32 fix inside NLLLoss2d.cu, but it was deferred for a separate change (I asked about it here: [my comment](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/197565#issuecomment-6193934238)). Happy to go with whichever scope the maintainers prefer.

items.title: Use atomic_cas inside a loop
items.author: giorgio-arena
items.body_excerpt:
Hi, I'm experimenting with a simple kernel that reduces a rank-3 tensor on its last dimension. The kernel uses atomics to sum across one tensor row (I know it's not efficient, this is just a simple reproducer). I'm using two versions of the atomics, the first using atomic_add, and the second using the lock-like mechanism with atomic_cas and atomic_xchg.

```
@triton.jit
def _sum_kernel(X, Locks, O, width: tl.constexpr, use_atomic_add: tl.constexpr):
  in_off = tl.program_id(0) * width
  out_off = tl.program_id(0)

  for w in range(0, width):
    x = tl.load(X + in_off + w)
    if use_atomic_add:
      tl.atomic_add(O + out_off, x)
    else:
      while tl.atomic_cas(Locks + out_off, 0, 1) == 1:
        pass
      tl.store(O + out_off, tl.load(O + out_off) + x)
      tl.atomic_xchg(Locks + out_off, 0)


def _sum_fn(a, use_atomic_add):
  b, h, w = a.shape
  locks = torch.zeros([b, h], dtype=torch.int32, device='cuda')
  out = torch.zeros([b, h], dtype=a.dtype, device='cuda')
  _sum_kernel[(b * h,)](a, locks, out, width=w, use_atomic_add=use_atomic_add)
  return out

if __name__ == "__main__":
  x = torch.empty((8, 64, 128), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda").normal_()
  ref = torch.sum(x, axis=-1)
  rtol = 1e-03

  print(torch.allclose(ref, _sum_fn(x, True), rtol=rtol))
  print(torch.allclose(ref, _sum_fn(x, False), rtol=rtol))
```

Unfortunately for the second version I get
```

  File "/usr/local/home/giorgio/triton/python/triton/compiler.py", line 741, in visit_For
    assert for_op_region.size() == 1, "We use SCF, so the loop body should only have one block"
AssertionError: We use SCF, so the loop body should only have one block
```

Any help would be appreciated, thanks.

Hi, I doubt this is a duplicate of https://github.com/openai/triton/issues/1058 because I am not overflowing on the program ids (largest PID should be `cdiv(8192, 16) * cdiv(8192, 32) = 131072` in my case).

I extended https://github.com/openai/triton/blob/main/python/triton/ops/matmul.py to support 4D tensors, e.g. of shapes (2, 8, 1024, 1024) and (2, 8, 1024, 512).

Is it an issue in my implementation or expected at first glance? I have no issues on smaller shapes. This is on A100-SXM4-80GB on triton `main`.

If `c_ptrs = c_ptr + N * offs_am[:, None] + 1 * offs_bn[None, :]`, which means the output of tl.dot is row major, the results are equal. items.title: Loop-carry detection skips `prev = cur` when both start as the same value, silently keeping the pre-loop value instead of carrying it
items.author: Hughshine
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug


**TL;DR.** `CodeGenerator._find_carries` decides which variables of a `for` or `while` loop become `iter_args` by comparing IR values after one dry run of the body, instead of asking whether a value can differ between iterations. If `prev` and `cur` are the same IR value before the loop and the loop runs `prev = cur`, `prev` looks unchanged and is not carried, so it keeps its pre-loop value in every iteration and after the loop. Regression from #7200, first in 3.5.0 (3.4.0 is right). Possible fix: also carry every name that is assigned in the loop (as 3.4.0 did), or only those that share their initial IR value with another name.

**Why one dry run misses it.** `_find_carries` ([L485-L524](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/6fe3348e6e907584e07e593ab19a35caee95c37a/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L485-L524), the comparison is [L513](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/6fe3348e6e907584e07e593ab19a35caee95c37a/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L513)) runs the body once with every name bound to its pre-loop value. When `prev = cur` runs there, `cur` is still at its pre-loop value, so `prev` is bound to the value it already had. In the real body `cur` is a block argument, so `prev = cur` is a different value in every iteration. Seeing that takes a second pass that already knows `cur` is carried.

The smallest example. `prev` is `cur`'s value at the start of each iteration; `SAME=False` is the control, where `prev` is equal to `cur` but a different IR value:

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(out_ptr, n, SAME: tl.constexpr):
    cur = 0
    if SAME:
        prev = cur          # prev and cur are the same IR value
    else:
        prev = cur + 0      # control: equal to cur, but a different IR value
    for i in range(n):
        prev = cur          # prev is cur's value at the start of the iteration
        cur = cur + 1
    tl.store(out_ptr, prev)      # expected n - 1
    tl.store(out_ptr + 1, cur)   # expected n


n = 5
for same in (True, False):
    out = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    k = kernel[(1, )](out, n, same)
    print(f"SAME={same!s:5} prev, cur = {out.tolist()}, expected {[n - 1, n]}")
    print("   ", [l.strip() for l in k.asm["ttir"].splitlines() if "scf.for" in l][0].split(" : ")[0])
```
```
SAME=True  prev, cur = [0, 5], expected [4, 5]
    %cur = scf.for %i = %c0_i32 to %n step %c1_i32 iter_args(%cur_0 = %c0_i32) -> (i32)
SAME=False prev, cur = [4, 5], expected [4, 5]
    %prev:2 = scf.for %i = %c0_i32 to %n step %c1_i32 iter_args(%cur = %c0_i32, %prev_0 = %c0_i32) -> (i32, i32)
```
With `SAME=True` only `cur` is an `iter_arg`. 3.4.0 has two `iter_args` in both cases and returns `[4, 5]`. Without an `iter_arg`, `prev` is still bound to its pre-loop value when the body starts, and `enter_sub_region` restores that binding when the loop ends ([L146](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/6fe3348e6e907584e07e593ab19a35caee95c37a/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L146)).

**Why since 3.5.0.** Up to 3.4.0 every name that is assigned in the loop and live before it was carried ([visit_For](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/d4432f6b89ef554007a53ef90f2499d90792d7e7/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L1114-L1115), [visit_While](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/d4432f6b89ef554007a53ef90f2499d90792d7e7/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L1153-L1154)). #7200 (2025-06-23, "Improve detection of loop carries", for builtins that modify their arguments) replaced that with the comparison of IR values; v3.5.0 is the first tag that contains it. The existing tests for shared initial values (`test_loop_carry_shared_initial_value` and its while and tuple variants in test_frontend.py, #11369) update the aliased variables independently (`a = a + 1`, `b = b + 2`), so none has a copy between them.

**Possible fix.** Two variants, both tested as source patches on main @6fe3348e6.

Carry every name that is assigned in the loop, as 3.4.0 did, and keep the comparison:
```diff
--- a/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py
+++ b/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py
@@ -493,6 +493,9 @@ class CodeGenerator(ast.NodeVisitor):
         self.scf_stack.pop()
         block.erase()
 
+        # A name that is assigned in the loop may have copied another one, which an unchanged handle doesn't show.
+        assigned = {n.id for n in ast.walk(node) if isinstance(n, ast.Name) and isinstance(n.ctx, ast.Store)}
+
         # If a variable (name) has changed value within the loop, then it's
         # a loop-carried variable. (The new and old value must be of the
         # same type)
@@ -510,7 +513,7 @@ class CodeGenerator(ast.NodeVisitor):
 
                 live_handles = flatten_values_to_ir([live_val])
                 loop_handles = flatten_values_to_ir([loop_val])
-                if live_handles != loop_handles:
+                if name in assigned or live_handles != loop_handles:
                     names.append(name)
                     init_tys.append(live_val.type)
                     init_handles.extend(live_handles)
```
The comparison was added by #7200 for builtins that modify their arguments in place. #8832 (2025-11-25) removed that case ("now that we ban mutations") together with its tests, attribute and item assignment raise, and aggregates cannot be assigned to after construction, so a name whose IR value changes is a name that is assigned. In test_frontend.py and the Gluon frontend tests, 57 of the 181 (name, loop) pairs that `_find_carries` looked at had a changed IR value, and all 57 are assigned in the loop. The set of assigned names comes from the AST, so it does not depend on what the dry run did; that also covers a branch that only the lowering takes (see below). It over-carries assigned names whose value does not change (`x = x`); they become `iter_args` and the canonicalizer in `make_ttir` removes them (the TTIR of t

items.title: Pipelining drops `volatile=True` and `cache_modifier=".cv"` on loads
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

In a pipelined loop, a load with `volatile=True` or `cache_modifier=".cv"` is turned into a `cp.async` copy, which drops the volatile / `.cv` semantics. The load is also issued `num_stages - 1` iterations early. With `num_stages=1` the PTX has `ld.volatile.global` / `ld.global.cv` as expected.

```python
import re
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(X, Y, NUM_STAGES: tl.constexpr, VOLATILE: tl.constexpr, CACHE: tl.constexpr):
    offs = tl.arange(0, 128)
    acc = tl.zeros([128], tl.float32)
    for i in tl.range(0, 8, num_stages=NUM_STAGES):
        acc += tl.load(X + i * 128 + offs, volatile=VOLATILE, cache_modifier=CACHE)
    tl.store(Y + offs, acc)


X, Y = torch.empty(1024, device="cuda"), torch.empty(128, device="cuda")
for volatile, cache, expected in ((True, "", "ld.volatile.global"), (False, ".cv", "ld.global.cv")):
    for num_stages in (1, 3):
        ptx = kernel.warmup(X, Y, num_stages, volatile, cache, grid=(1, )).asm["ptx"]
        print(f"volatile={volatile} cache_modifier={cache!r} num_stages={num_stages}: "
              f"{expected} x{len(re.findall(re.escape(expected), ptx))}, cp.async x{len(re.findall(r'cp\.async\.c[ag]', ptx))}")
```

```
volatile=True cache_modifier='' num_stages=1: ld.volatile.global x8, cp.async x0
volatile=True cache_modifier='' num_stages=3: ld.volatile.global x0, cp.async x10
volatile=False cache_modifier='.cv' num_stages=1: ld.global.cv x8, cp.async x0
volatile=False cache_modifier='.cv' num_stages=3: ld.global.cv x0, cp.async x10
```

`AssignLatencies` does not exclude volatile loads or `.cv` loads from pipelining. `LowerLoops` passes `isVolatile` to `AsyncCopyGlobalToLocalOp`, but its NVIDIA lowering never reads it and maps the cache modifier to `cp.async.ca` / `.cg`. A volatile load polling a flag written by another CTA would then read a stale value, prefetched iterations earlier. I only have PTX-level evidence; I did not observe a stale read in a spin test on this GPU.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8
