items.title: [inductor] Compile worker pool can lose a job when it re-forks right after a quiesce
items.author: yyming009
items.body_excerpt:
（Update: the proposed fix below has a flaw; see the correction in the comments.） ### 🐛 Describe the bug We found the issue that Multi-node training in miles hangs at step 1 because an Inductor compilation task on one rank never returns ([radixark/miles#4046](https://github.com/radixark/miles/issues/4046)). The compiler process pool shuts down after 60 seconds of inactivity and forks new workers for the next compilation; if that fork happens during the tens-of-milliseconds window when the old pool is shutting down, a new worker inherits a locked lock and hangs forever. I’ve run the reproduction script below myself, and the patch is ready—I’ll open a PR once the issue is marked actionable. The analysis in the collapsed section below was prepared by an AI assistant and reviewed by me. **Minimal repro** (CPU only, standard library; it mirrors `SubprocMain._start_pool` and `SubprocMain._quiesce`): ```python # CPython 3.12, Linux or macOS: prints "job lost" after 10 s. # With old.shutdown(wait=True) in place of the lock.acquire() line, it prints "ok". import concurrent.futures as cf, multiprocessing as mp, multiprocessing.util as mpu, os, sys ctx = mp.get_context("fork") old = cf.ProcessPoolExecutor(2, mp_context=ctx) old.submit(int).result() mpu.Finalize(None, old.shutdown, exitpriority=sys.maxsize) # SubprocMain._start_pool old.shutdown(wait=False) # SubprocMain._quiesce lock = old._shutdown_lock; lock.acquire() # the manager thread, mid-join old = None new = cf.ProcessPoolExecutor(2, mp_context=ctx) # the next SubprocMain._start_pool try: print("ok", new.submit(os.getpid).result(timeout=10), flush=True) except cf.TimeoutError: print("job lost: workers stuck in concurrent/futures/process.py weakref_cb", flush=True) for p in mp.active_children(): # the stuck workers never exit on their own p.kill() os._exit(0) ```
AI-assisted analysis (drafted with an AI coding assistant from our logs, stack dumps and experiments; reviewed by me) ### Mechanism - With `quiesce_async_compile_pool` on (the default), the compile sidecar calls `pool.shutdown(wait=False)` after `quiesce_async_compile_time` (60 s) without results. The next WAKEUP or JOB forks a new pool (`SubprocMain._start_pool` → `_warm_process_pool`). - CPython 3.12 holds the old executor's `_shutdown_lock` in `_ExecutorManagerThread.join_executor_internals()` while it joins the old workers, a window of tens of milliseconds. Every worker of a pool forked in that window inherits the lock in the held state. - `_start_pool` registers `multiprocessing.util.Finalize(None, self.pool.shutdown, exitpriority=sys.maxsize)`, and the quiesce never cancels it, so the old executor stays reachable. When it is collected inside the new worker (in multiprocessing's `_after_fork()` or in a later GC), its weakref callback runs `with shutdown_lock: thread_wakeup.wakeup()` and blocks forever. - The job that worker took never returns, so `AsyncCompile.wait` waits forever. - We believe this is also why `test_quiesce_repeatedly` is flaky and disabled on Linux (#176968). We have not checked CPython versions other than 3.12. ### Impact - Multi-node training (radixark/miles#4046), 32 ranks with a 32-worker pool each: about 1 in 8 runs hung in the first training step. The rank whose compile job was lost never issued its next collective, and its peers blocked in NCCL until the watchdog aborted the job an hour later. - With `quiesce_async_compile_time` lowered to 2 s, 6 attempts per arm on the same inputs: | arm | hung | |---|---| | default (quiesce on) | 4 of 6 | | `TORCHINDUCTOR_QUIESCE_ASYNC_COMPILE_POOL=0` | 0 of 6 | | join the old pool before forking | 0 of 6 | - Every hang traced to a fork 0–52 ms after a quiesce, with the old lock still held. py-spy showed the stuck worker in `concurrent/futures/process.py:312 weakref_cb`, during an import inside `_worker_compile_triton`. ### Proposed fix - On quiesce, keep the old pool and its finalizer. Before `_start_pool` forks a new pool, join the old one with `shutdown(wait=True)` and cancel its finalizer. The quiesce itself stays non-blocking, and `_shutdown_pool(terminate_workers=True)` also terminates an old pool that has not been joined yet. - The patch changes `torch/_inductor/compile_worker/subproc_pool.py` (+33/−5) and adds a regression test to `test/inductor/test_compile_worker.py` that fails on main and passes with the patch. - Alternatives: join at quiesce time (simpler, but it blocks the sidecar's message loop until the old workers exit), or use `forkserver`/`spawn` for re-created pools (cf. #148651, #108586). ### Workarounds `TORCHINDUCTOR_QUIESCE_ASYNC_COMPILE_POOL=0`, or `TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1`.
### Error logs _No response_ ### Versions ``` # Original hang (multi-node training): Linux x86_64, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CPython 3.12.3 # The CPU repro above, run on: Collecting environment information... PyTorch version: 2.11.0 Is debug build: False CUDA used to build PyTorch: None ROCM used to build PyTorch: N/A OS: macOS 26.7.1 (arm64) GCC version: Could not collect Clang version: 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2) CMake version: Could not collect Libc version: N/A Python version: 3.12.7 (main, Nov 15 2024, 17:32:29) [Clang 16.0.0 (clang-1600.0.26.4)] (64-bit runtime) Python platform: macOS-26.7.1-arm64-arm-64bit Is CUDA available: False CUDA runtime version: No CUDA CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to: N/A GPU models and configuration: No CUDA Nvidia driver version: No CUDA cuDNN version: No CUDA Is XPU available: False HIP runtime version: N/A MIOpen runtime version: N/A Is XNNPACK available: True Caching allocator config: N/A CPU: Apple M2 Pro Versions of relevant libraries: [pip3] Could not collect [conda] numpy 1.26.4 py312h7f4fdc5_0 [conda] numpy-base 1.26.4 py312he047099_0 [conda] numpydoc

items.title: [Perf][SM103] Mamba2 SSD chunked prefill 1.34–1.38x behind in-tree Triton at the 64-head shard; no causal-conv1d kernel
items.author: brandonfzhang
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

At Nemotron-3-Ultra's TP4 shard geometry (nheads 64, head_dim 64, d_state 128,
ngroups 2), FlashInfer's SSD chunked-prefill kernel runs **1.34–1.38x behind vLLM's
in-tree Triton chunk-scan on all 66 captured classes**. The verdict is
shard-geometry-sensitive: at the TP2 shard (nheads 128) FI is **1.19x ahead** on all
351 classes — so the gap is specific to the narrower per-rank head count, not the op.
Separately, FlashInfer ships no causal-conv1d kernel at any version we tested, so the
conv stage of the Mamba2 block always stays on the framework kernel even where FI
wins the SSM stage.

## Environment

- NVIDIA GB300 (SM103); CUDA 13.0; FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5
- Timing: CUPTI, 20 interleaved rounds, SM clock locked 2070 MHz, fp64 gates
  (measured at SSM-stage granularity; conv stage excluded for every candidate)
- Shapes from live serving of the published Nemotron-3-Ultra GB300 recipes
  (vLLM TP4 and SGLang TP2 legs)

## Exact call parameters

SSD chunked prefill: `nheads=64`, `head_dim=64`, `d_state=128`, `ngroups=2`,
`chunk_size=128`, `batch=1` varlen (T = total tokens in the call), bf16
activations. TP2 contrast rows use `nheads=128`, all else equal.

## Measurements — TP4 shard: nheads 64, head_dim 64, d_state 128, ngroups 2 (µs)

| chunk tokens | FI `ssd` | vLLM Triton chunk-scan | FI behind |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8480 | 449.7 | 336.8 | 1.34x |
| 16536–16960 | 862.7–878.8 | 630.5–644.9 | 1.36–1.38x |
| 25440 | 1307.8 | 951.0 | 1.38x |

Contrast, TP2 shard (nheads 128, same op): FI 1.19x ahead GPU-time-weighted, all
classes. Decode (selective-state-update) is competitive at both shards and ahead at
the speculative q=6 regime.

## Ask

1. Close the SSD chunk-scan gap at the 64-head shard (tiling for the half-width
   head count looks like the lever, given the 128-head win).
2. Ship a causal-conv1d kernel so the Mamba2 block can run FI end-to-end; today the
   conv stage forces a framework-kernel dependency regardless of SSM-stage wins.

## Related

- #3775 (selective_state_update_sm100 not AOT-registered)

items.title: [Bug] FlashInfer autotune cache is discarded every boot under MoE expert parallelism (EP>1): per-rank shapes never agree, so the fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn each start
items.author: ntxf31415
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

`_drop_diverged_autotune_cache()` discards the whole FlashInfer autotune cache — on every boot — whenever the per-rank MoE GEMM shapes differ, which is the normal case with **expert parallelism (EP > 1)**. The cache is then re-tuned from scratch each start, so the fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn every boot. Since the tactic selection is timing-based, end-to-end throughput varies across boots with identical config.

### Environment

- 4× GB10 (DGX Spark), SGLang TP4 / EP2, switchless RoCE ring
- MoE runner backend `flashinfer_mxfp4` (MXFP4 experts), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`
- FlashInfer 0.6.18, CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 92000

### Root cause

`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/flashinfer_autotune.py`:

```python
def _autotune_cache_digest(cache_path, env):
    ...
    payload = {"file": configs, "env": env}
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()

def _drop_diverged_autotune_cache(cache_path, group, env) -> None:
    digests = [""] * torch.distributed.get_world_size(group)
    torch.distributed.all_gather_object(digests, _autotune_cache_digest(cache_path, env), group=group)
    if len(set(digests)) == 1:
        return
    ...
    cache_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)          # <-- deletes the cache
```

Each rank digests **its own** `rank_tp{N}_pp0_dp0.json` and all four are compared. Under EP sharding each rank owns a different slice of the routed experts, so **the MoE GEMM problem shapes themselves differ per rank** and the files can never be equal. Measured on our four ranks (same boot, same config, caches cleared so all four start from empty):

| rank | distinct shapes in its cache | example expert shape present |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 24 | `(192, 2304, 320)` |
| 1 | 24 | `(64, 2304, 320)` |
| 2 | 24 | `(64, 2304, 320)` / `(192, …)` |
| 3 | 24 | `(16, 5120)`, `(4, 5120)` |

**The intersection of the four shape sets is empty.** So `len(set(digests)) == 1` is never true, the cache is `unlink`ed on every start, and every start re-profiles `trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1` / `gemm2` for all shapes.

Startup log, one boot:

```
Running FlashInfer autotune with cache: /root/.cache/sglang/flashinfer/autotune/0.6.18/sm121/<key>/rank_tp3_pp0_dp0.json
[AutoTuner]: Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1:   0%|          | 0/8 ...
```

Tuning count is **26–27 profiles per boot** regardless of whether a complete cache file is already present at that path. The shipped image cache contains only `sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4` entries, so the fused-MoE shapes always miss anyway.

Note the digest also includes the environment, so even equal tactics would not be enough — but here the file contents themselves cannot match.

### Impact

The fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn on every start, and it matters a lot. Two consecutive boots of the same configuration, measured with a cold single-stream prefill probe at 8K tokens:

| boot | prefill t/s (8K) |
|---|---|
| A | 3169 |
| B | 2431 |

**−23 % at 8K**, while 100K was essentially unchanged (3266 vs 3164) — i.e. the draw is shape-range dependent, and a bad draw is stable for the whole life of that process. We also saw a full 1.5× swing on longer inputs between boots.

### Workaround we run

We mount a site-patched copy of this file that keeps the digest check and the log line but drops the `unlink`:

```python
    log_info_on_rank0(logger, "[site patch] keeping per-rank autotune caches")
```

With the per-rank caches kept, subsequent boots report **0 tuning profiles** (cache genuinely read and used) and throughput is stable.

⚠️ Caveat we found the hard way: this is only safe if every rank's own cache is **complete**. If some ranks hit and others miss, the missing ranks enter the timing-reduction collective while the others don't — we reproduced that as an NCCL collective timeout at startup with the process hanging, so a partial cache is worse than none.

### Possible fix directions

1. Compare like-for-like per rank (i.e. make the guard per-rank rather than requiring cross-rank equality), given that under EP the shape sets legitimately differ.
2. Or key the digest only on the *tactics for the shapes this rank actually uses*, rather than on the whole file.
3. Or make the reduction group follow the ranks that actually share a shape set.

If the divergence check is load-bearing for a reason we have not understood, it may be worth at least not deleting — logging and continuing — so a partially-cached fleet degrades to slow rather than to a hang.

items.title: [CI] Runner 5090-vast-no-0 is out of disk: every job fails in Install dependencies with 'No space left on device'
items.author: nvpohanh
items.body_excerpt:
[by Claude Code]

## Summary

The self-hosted runner **`5090-vast-no-0`** (label `1-gpu-5090`) is out of disk space. Since about **2026-10-15 08:50 UTC**, every job it picked up has failed in the `Install dependencies` step with `No space left on device (os error 28)`, about one minute after starting.

A failed job frees the runner within a minute, so it immediately takes the next queued `1-gpu-5090` job. It has been absorbing a large share of the 1-GPU-small jobs across many PRs, and reruns keep landing on it. Every failing job we checked ran on this one host. Jobs on other 5090 hosts (for example `5090-vast-hu-0`, `5090-vast-hu-3`) install fine.

These are also tracked in the flaky tracker #42752 as rows I27, I28, and I29.

## Failure signature

`uv` fails while installing the CI venv into `/opt/sglang-ci-py3.12` (usually while unpacking `numba`), or while writing into `/root/.cache/uv`:

```
error: Failed to install: numba-0.65.1-cp312-cp312-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl (numba==0.65.1)
  cause: Failed to copy to `/opt/sglang-ci-py3.12/lib/python3.12/site-packages/numba/tests/test_parfors.py`
  cause: No space left on device (os error 28)

```

```
cause: failed to write to file `/root/.cache/uv/.tmpSb5MIP/sgl_kernel/sm90/common_ops.abi3.so`: No space left on device (os error 28)
```

## Root cause

**Confirmed:** the filesystem that holds `/opt/sglang-ci-py3.12` and `/root/.cache/uv` on `5090-vast-no-0` is full. The failure is specific to this host and does not depend on the PR.

**Not confirmed:** what filled it. Likely candidates are a growing uv or Hugging Face cache, leftover CI venvs, or core dumps (`SGLANG_CUDA_COREDUMP=1` is set in CI). This needs someone with access to the host.

## Proposed fix

1. Take `5090-vast-no-0` out of the `1-gpu-5090` pool (or stop its runner service) right away, so it stops absorbing jobs.
2. Free disk space on the host (uv cache, HF cache, stale venvs, core dumps), then put it back in the pool.
3. Optionally, add a free-disk-space check before `Install dependencies` that fails fast with a clear message, or have the runner deregister itself when the disk is nearly full, so a full host can't keep taking jobs.

items.title: [WS] getPartitionOutputs assertion in NVWSHoistTmemStore with warp_specialize=True on a pointer-load persistent matmul
items.author: builtin-pb
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Compiling the kernel below for Blackwell (`cuda:100` or `cuda:103`) stops with an internal assertion when the outer tile loop uses `tl.range(..., warp_specialize=True)`, the inner K loop uses plain pointer loads and `tl.dot`, and C is written with a plain `tl.store`:

```
Partitioning.cpp:24: ... mlir::triton::gpu::getPartitionOutputs(mlir::Operation*): Assertion `op->hasAttr(kPartitionOutputsAttrName)' failed.
... Pipeline failed while executing [`TritonGPUAutomaticWarpSpecialization` on 'builtin.module' operation, `NVWSHoistTmemStore` on 'builtin.module' operation]
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

This reproduces on Triton 3.8.0 (PyPI wheel; there the assertion is at `Partition.cpp:354`) and on main (`0d4e0a0c`). It is compile-only and needs no GPU; the kernel is never launched (it assumes full tiles and 16-byte-aligned, contiguous fp16 A and B and fp32 C). We are not asking for this loop to be specialized, only for no assertion: `warp_specialize` is documented as an attempt, and loops it cannot partition are otherwise left alone, as with the controls below. Triton's own `test_warp_specialize_tma_matmul_persistent` has the same structure with pointer loads for A and B and expects `ttg.warp_specialize`; it differs only in storing C through a descriptor.

### Reproducer

```python
"""Compile-only reproducer (no GPU needed).

Requesting automatic warp specialization on a persistent tile loop whose body is
an ordinary pointer-load matmul makes Triton hit an internal assertion:
    getPartitionOutputs: Assertion `op->hasAttr(kPartitionOutputsAttrName)' failed.

    python ws_assert_min.py              # warp_specialize=True: assertion
    python ws_assert_min.py --ws 0       # same kernel without it: compiles

--inner 0 drops the inner K loop (one tl.dot per tile); --dot 0 replaces tl.dot
with row/column sums; --cdesc 1 stores C through a TMA tensor descriptor
(as Triton's own persistent warp-specialization test does); --arch picks the target (100 = B200, 103 = B300, 90 = H100);
--warps and --stages set num_warps (default 4) and num_stages (default 3).
"""
import argparse
import inspect

import triton
import triton.language as tl
from triton.backends.compiler import GPUTarget
from triton.compiler import ASTSource


@triton.jit
def ws_min(A, B, C, num_tiles, k_iters,
           BM: tl.constexpr, BN: tl.constexpr, BK: tl.constexpr,
           WS: tl.constexpr, INNER: tl.constexpr, DOT: tl.constexpr, CDESC: tl.constexpr):
    rm = tl.arange(0, BM)
    rn = tl.arange(0, BN)
    rk = tl.arange(0, BK)
    K = k_iters * BK
    if CDESC:
        c_desc = tl.make_tensor_descriptor(C, shape=[num_tiles * BM, BN], strides=[BN, 1], block_shape=[BM, BN])
    for tile in tl.range(tl.program_id(0), num_tiles, tl.num_programs(0), warp_specialize=WS):
        rows = tile * BM + rm
        acc = tl.zeros((BM, BN), tl.float32)
        if INNER:
            for k in range(k_iters):
                a = tl.load(A + rows[:, None] * K + (k * BK + rk)[None, :])
                b = tl.load(B + (k * BK + rk)[:, None] * BN + rn[None, :])
                if DOT:
                    acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc)
                else:
                    acc += tl.sum(a.to(tl.float32), 1)[:, None] + tl.sum(b.to(tl.float32), 0)[None, :]
        else:
            a = tl.load(A + rows[:, None] * K + rk[None, :])
            b = tl.load(B + rk[:, None] * BN + rn[None, :])
            if DOT:
                acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc)
            else:
                acc += tl.sum(a.to(tl.float32), 1)[:, None] + tl.sum(b.to(tl.float32), 0)[None, :]
        if CDESC:
            c_desc.store([tile * BM, 0], acc)
        else:
            tl.store(C + rows[:, None] * BN + rn[None, :], acc)


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--ws", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--inner", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--dot", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--cdesc", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--arch", type=int, default=100)
    p.add_argument("--warps", type=int, default=4)
    p.add_argument("--stages", type=int, default=3)
    args = p.parse_args()

    constants = dict(BM=128, BN=64, BK=64, WS=bool(args.ws), INNER=bool(args.inner), DOT=bool(args.dot), CDESC=bool(args.cdesc))
    runtime = dict(A="*fp16", B="*fp16", C="*fp32", num_tiles="i32", k_iters="i32")
    names = list(ws_min.arg_names)
    signature = {n: runtime.get(n, "constexpr") for n in names}
    attrs = {(names.index(n),): [["tt.divisibility", 16]] for n in ("A", "B", "C")}
    key = "constexprs" if "constexprs" in inspect.signature(ASTSource).parameters else "constants"
    src = ASTSource(ws_min, signature=signature, attrs=attrs, **{key: constants})
    print(f"triton {triton.__version__}, target cuda:{args.arch}, warps {args.warps}, stages {args.stages}, {constants}", flush=True)
    compiled = triton.compile(src, target=GPUTarget("cuda", args.arch, 32),
                              options=dict(num_warps=args.warps, num_stages=args.stages))
    ttgir = compiled.asm["ttgir"]
    print("COMPILED; ttg.warp_specialize ops in TTGIR:", ttgir.count("ttg.warp_specialize("), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

| Command (`--arch 100` or `--arch 103`) | 3.8.0 and main |
|---|---|
| `python ws_assert_min.py` (also with `--stages 1` or `--warps 8`) | assertion |
| `--ws 0` | compiles |
| `--cdesc 1` (C stored through a tensor descriptor) | compiles and emits one `ttg.warp_specialize` |
| `--inner 0` or `--dot 0` | compiles, without specialization |

<details><summary>Full output on main, including the MLIR reproducer</summary>

```
python: triton/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/IR/Partitioning.cpp:24: llvm::SmallVector<llvm::SetVector<int, llvm::SmallVector<int, 0>, llvm::DenseSet<int, llvm::DenseMapInfo<int, void> >, 0>, 4> mlir::triton::gpu::getPartitionOutputs(mlir::Operation*): Assertion `op->hasAttr(kPartitionOutputsAttrName)' failed.
module {
  tt.func public @ws_min(%ar

items.title: [Bug][Gateway] Add missing reserved routes for supported Messages and Audio APIs
items.author: googs1025
items.body_excerpt:
Parent issue: #2989

## Problem

The Gateway request parser and ModelRouter already support:

- `/v1/messages`
- `/v1/audio/transcriptions`
- `/v1/audio/translations`

However, these paths are missing from the deployed shared `reserved-router` in `config/gateway/gateway-plugin/gateway-plugin.yaml`.

A request must first match this route to enter the external processing service. The plugin then extracts the model from the request body, writes the internal routing headers, clears the route cache, and rematches the request onto a model route.

Without the first route, the existing parser and ModelRouter support do not form a complete deployment path.

## Proposed change

Add these existing endpoints to the shared reserved route:

```yaml
- path:
    type: PathPrefix
    value: /v1/messages
- path:
    type: PathPrefix
    value: /v1/audio/transcriptions
- path:
    type: PathPrefix
    value: /v1/audio/translations
```

Verify the rendered Kustomize output as well.

## Testing

Add regression tests confirming that:

- all three paths are present in the shared reserved route;
- all three paths use the shared Gateway ext_proc policy;
- `/v1/messages` reaches JSON request-body processing;
- the two audio paths reach multipart request-body processing;
- query strings do not break routing;
- existing Chat, Responses, and Videos routes remain unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Do not change `PathPrefix` to `Exact`.
- Do not add HTTP method matches.
- Do not introduce an endpoint registry.
- Do not add `/v1/audio/speech`; that is tracked separately.
- Do not refactor the existing request dispatcher.

## Acceptance criteria

- Messages requests complete the reserved-route -> ext_proc -> model-route flow.
- Audio transcription and translation requests can extract the multipart model and select a backend Pod.
- Existing routes retain their current behavior.
- Regression tests cover both the deployed route and request-processing entry points.

items.title: [RFC]: A standard for MonoKernels in vllm/models
items.author: dllehr-amd
items.body_excerpt:
### Motivation.

A **MonoKernel** is a persistent kernel that runs most or all of one decoder layer's decode step in a single launch. This RFC proposes one way to add them under `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/`:

- The layer loop calls `mono.forward_layer(...)`, which launches the layer's kernel or calls the vLLM layer unchanged. The module tree and parameter names never change.
- A shared library, `vllm/models/common/mono/` (~650 lines), owns what every MonoKernel repeats: refusals, routing, fail-stop, health words, peer memory, cache re-binding.
- A model adds its kernel plus ~400 lines, instead of a 6–24k-line stack of its own.

The standard starts ROCm-only, where all known MonoKernels live (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-M3, Kimi-K3). CUDA joins with a CUDA co-author.

#### Why MonoKernels

At low concurrency, decode is bound by launch overhead and weight reads, and a MonoKernel removes most of both. On 8× MI350X a graph-mode GLM-5.2 decode step issues ~2,459 kernels in vLLM. With the MonoKernel it issues ~210: 75 MonoKernel launches plus ~135 for dense layers 0–2, input prep and the head.
 
| GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (#60889), TP8, MI350X, ~3k-token context | vLLM | MonoKernel | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Time per token, batch 1 / 8, defaults (BF16 attention) | 13.70 / 17.33 ms | 5.92 / 11.44 ms | 2.31× / 1.51× |
| Time per token, batch 1, FP8 attention opt-in | 13.70 ms | 4.80 ms | 2.85× |
| MoE layer w/o indexer (57 of 75), batch 4 / 8, FP8 | 178.8 / 189.6 µs | 69.1 / 100.6 µs | 2.59× / 1.88× |
| MoE layer with indexer (18 of 75), batch 4 / 8, FP8 | 214.9 / 227.6 µs | 88.5 / 123.4 µs | 2.43× / 1.84× |
| AgentX time between tokens, 1 / 8 users (3,600 s/point), FP8 | 15.0 / 20.4 ms | 6.5 / 12.7 ms | 2.28× / 1.68× |
| GSM8K strict, 1,319 questions, graphs, BF16 | 1228, 1234, 1235 (3 runs) | 1240 | parity: paired McNemar p = 0.22–0.63 |

Layer times are profiler-corrected, from one run. The gain shrinks with batch size, so the target is latency-bound serving: agents, chat and small-batch decode.

The cost is code, mostly runtime that each implementation rebuilds. Counts are `.py` lines, tests excluded:

### Proposed Change.

#### Goals and non-goals

**Goals:** a new MonoKernel should cost its kernel plus a few hundred lines, and be as safe as the first one.

1. One pattern: a per-model spec plus one routing call in the layer loop.
2. Reliable, work consistently across default shapes, sizes etc.  (no temperature 0, isl restrictions etc)
3. Off by default, to with one flag: `--monokernel`. The only shared files a model touches are its `model.py`, one CI job entry, one CODEOWNERS line, and any vLLM cache feature its kernel needs that doesn't exist yet (e.g. Kimi-K3's FP16 recurrent state).
4. Weight loading tries to be identical to non-mono paths, exception use cases are acceptable, however, we should avoid duplicating entire layer weight formats.
5. Functionally equivalent to default decode layers. 
6. Reviewable: every PR has the same CI tests and the same report.

**Not in Scope**

- Prefill and mixed steps. These always run vLLM's layers.
- Models compiled with `@support_torch_compile`.
- Launches that span more than two layer (some fusions may fuse end of one layer with beginning of another)
- No Runtime fallback. If a megakernel fails the engine should stop.

#### Design

##### Layout

Nothing below `<vendor>/` branches on platform. RFC #42770 makes the vendor `__init__.py` the only switch. Paths below are relative to `vllm/models/` except `tests/`.

| Path | Holds | 
| --- | --- |
| `tests/models/common/mono/` | Test kit: fake configs, fake kernel, golden-layer checker, fault harness |
| `<model>/<vendor>/mono/spec.py` | The model's `MonoSpec` |
| `<model>/<vendor>/mono/weights.py` | Packs weights into the kernel layout |
| `<model>/<vendor>/mono/kernel.py` | Cache binding, eligibility, build per width, launch |
| `<model>/<vendor>/model.py` | The hook | 
| `<model>/<vendor>/ops/mono/` | Kernel source | 
| `tests/models/<model>/<vendor>_mono/` | Model CI tests |


##### Interface

The model names its spec by import path, so config-time code can read the spec without importing the model.

```python
# vllm/models/common/mono/spec.py
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MonoSpec:
    name: str                                          # config value and log name
    layers: Callable[[PretrainedConfig], list[int]]    # decoder layers that get a kernel
    widths: tuple[int, ...]                            # rows per launch, built and tested
    supports: frozenset[Feature]                       # features in use but not listed are refused
    caches: Mapping[str, CacheReq]                     # KV / index / state caches per layer: group, dtype, layout
    weight_source: Literal["views", "convert"]         # convert: once after load, original freed
    options: Mapping[str, Any]                         # declared opt-ins and tuning defaults, e.g. fp8_attention
    refuse_config: Callable[[VllmConfig], list[str]]   # before load
    refuse_model: Callable[[nn.Module], list[str]]     # after load
    pack: Callable[[nn.Module, MonoContext], Any]      # weights, once
    bind: Callable[[MonoContext, Mapping[str, torch.Tensor]], list[str]]  # caches, at every re-bind
    eligible: Callable[[MonoContext, MonoStep], str | None]   # per-step no-go reason
    build: Callable[[MonoContext, Any, nn.Module, int], LayerKernel]  # packed, the vLLM layer, width

class LayerKernel(Protocol):
    def launch(self, step: MonoStep, *args, **kwargs) -> Any: ...  # returns what the vLLM layer returns
    def health(self) -> torch.Tensor: ...              # error words, layout from abi.py
```

```python
# vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/model.py
class XForCausalLM(nn.Module, SupportsMonoKernel):
    mono_spec = "vllm.models.<model>.<vendor>.mono.spec:MONO_SPEC"

    def process_weights_after_loading(self):
        # pack weights, build kernels for this rank's layers; None when the switch is off
        self.model.mo

items.title: [Feature] Carry the next-token embedding row in the distributed sampling exchange (no separate embedding collective)
items.author: goyalayus
items.body_excerpt:
Shard the input embedding with the same vocab partition as the vocab-parallel LM head; during the distributed argmax/sampling exchange each rank attaches the embedding row of its local winner, so every rank gets the next-token embedding together with the token and the separate embedding all-reduce/broadcast disappears.
Vs. a replicated table this saves memory (~1.1 GB/GPU for a 154880x4096 BF16 table at TP8); vs. the current vocab-parallel all-reduce it saves one collective per decode step, which matters most on PCIe-only / memory-tight TP (temperature sampling stays exact via Gumbel-max; top-k/top-p, prefill and injected tokens fall back to the existing path).

items.title: [Performance]: Kimi K3 fused attention-residual epilogue is skipped for speculative verify steps (token ceiling defaults to 1)
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

In `modeling_kimi_linear.py`, `_apply_attn_res_add_and_rmsnorm()` / `_apply_attn_res_and_rmsnorm()` take the fused ops (`trtllm::attn_res_add_rmsnorm_fwd`, `trtllm::attn_res_rmsnorm_fwd`) only for `M <= _FUSED_ATTN_RES_MAX_TOKENS`. With the default `KIMI_K3_ATTN_RES_TOPOLOGY=per_token`, `_read_fused_attn_res_max_tokens()` resolves the ceiling to 1, so only single-token decode steps are fused. A speculative-decoding verify step (e.g. 1 + 7 draft tokens, M = 8 per rank) and any decode batch of more than one request fall back to torch add + `attn_res_fwd` + RMSNorm at every layer: in an nsys trace of one Kimi K3 + DSpark verify step that is about 186 `attn_res` + 188 RMSNorm + ~270 add kernels. Under `split`, the same per-token kernels are already used up to 32 tokens ("the top of the measured range").

Measured on SM107 (single GPU, model helper functions in a CUDA graph, M = 8, N = 2..12 snapshots):

| op | unfused | fused |
|---|---|---|
| add + attn_res + RMSNorm | 6.6-9.0 us | 3.4-4.3 us |
| attn_res + RMSNorm | 5.3-7.7 us | 3.0-4.2 us |

M = 16 is the same. The updated prefix is bit-identical; the normalized output differs from the unfused chain by 2-25 bf16 ulps (max abs 0.016-0.031 at |x| ~ 4), the same as the fused path that M = 1 decode already uses by default.

End to end (Kimi K3 + DSpark, 7 drafts, 8 GPUs over 2 nodes, SM107, single request) with `KIMI_K3_FUSED_ATTN_RES_MAX_TOKENS=32`, together with a small unrelated double-add fusion worth about 0.1 ms: decode step -0.59 ms at 2K context, -0.53 ms at 32K and 128K. Speculative acceptance unchanged over ~825 requests; our quality checks unchanged apart from one numerics-sensitive item that also flips between cold starts.

Proposal: default the ceiling to 32 for every topology. `KIMI_K3_FUSED_ATTN_RES=0` keeps the unfused path, and the variable still overrides the ceiling. PR to follow.

cc @reasonsolo (#19182)

items.title: Feature Request: KV snapshot for agent fan-out: use seq_cp at divergence points
items.author: Winamin
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

I use llama.cpp version:

```
version: 0.4.0-dev (build 10889, commit 311d4211b)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
```

I'd like to discuss a possible use of  seq_cp as a general caching primitive, beyond fork and speculative decoding.

During prefill, when the sequence reaches the point where two agents will diverge, I copy the full KV state into a spare sequence with `llama_memory_seq_cp`. When a sibling agent arrives later, its prompt is matched against stored token sequences, and the snapshot is restored wholesale with another `seq_cp`.

This extends `seq_cp` from fork and speculative decoding to a general caching primitive.

### Motivation

In Claude Code and other agent scenarios, a parent agent can concurrently spawn multiple sibling agents (fan-out). They share a long parent context (intermediate prefix) and then branch off to perform different tasks.

But existing prefix caching doesn't help. Sibling agents aren't extensions of each other — they share an intermediate prefix, not a prefix starting from position 0. So each agent has to prefill the entire shared context again.

Measured on one real session of 20 requests, RTX 5060 Ti, 9B Q4, llama.cpp:

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| session requests served by a cache layer | 15 / 20 |
| prompt tokens never forwarded | 447657 / 591946 (75.6%) |
| cold prefill, median | 2,004 ctx tok/s |
| cache-reused, median | 24,368 ctx tok/s |
| cache-reused, best | 52039 ctx tok/s |
| reply of 30-106 tokens, cold | 22646 forwarded, 11.3 s |
| reply of 30-106 tokens, archive | 1055 forwarded, 2.0 s |
| reply of 30-106 tokens, in-sequence | 77 forwarded, 1.0 s |

A 52039-token prompt, 51962 of it served from cache, 77 forwarded, 1.0 s.
So prefill/decode split reads zero on the batched path; only the total is real. 

About 12x at the median. Without this mechanism, the same 5-agent fan-out causes every sibling to re-prefill the shared 20k-60k token context, pushing wall time into the tens of minutes.

### Possible Implementation

This mechanism only uses public APIs and doesn’t require modifying the core llama.cpp code.


```c
// snapshot on the way past the divergence point: the chat template's
// user-turn marker if there is one, otherwise the first token where the
// prompt diverges from what the sequence holds.
llama_memory_seq_cp(ctx, src_seq, archive_slot, 0, -1);

// restore: longest strict prefix match wins.
llama_memory_seq_rm(ctx, dst_seq, 0, -1);
llama_memory_seq_cp(ctx, archive_slot, dst_seq, 0, -1);
```


Reference implementation: https://github.com/Winamin/cc_srv
Charts and data in the README; edit the DLL and model paths in lib.py to run it.

items.title: [RFC] Review MC_USE_TENT=1 gaps for classic TE callers
items.author: staryxchen
items.body_excerpt:
## How this list was produced

Started as a static pass over:

- the C++ shim (`mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transfer_engine.cpp`, `use_tent_` branches)
- the Python wrapper (`mooncake-integration/transfer_engine/transfer_engine_py.cpp`)
- inference-engine call sites that use `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`

Local runtime (2026-09-10, installed TENT wheel, 1P1D PD) then confirmed
some items and left others unverified. Status below is as of **2026-09-17**
(`origin/main` `c4d632888b`). Please still reproduce on your tree before
treating a remaining item as confirmed.

## Why the compatibility layer

We are wiring inference engines to TENT's **native** APIs, but that work is
not finished. Until it is, we use the classic TE compatibility layer
(`MC_USE_TENT=1`) to validate TENT **runtime** stability against existing
callers (PD disaggregation and others). This RFC tracks gaps in that layer.
It is not the native-API migration itself.

## Summary

`MC_USE_TENT=1` (and `MC_USE_TEV1=1`) is meant to run existing
`mooncake::TransferEngine` / `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine` code on the TENT
runtime. Register + sync submit/poll are wired up enough for PD KV transfer.

PD happy path **works** under `MC_USE_TENT=1` (local 1P1D Qwen3-4B
`/generate` 200). This RFC is not a claim that PD is broken today.

Most of the original P0/P1/P2 shim holes now have merged PRs. What is still
open is protocol pinning for `efa`/`ascend`, Python sync/poll semantics, and
`installTransport()` returning `nullptr` for classic C/Go/EFA callers.

If you find a **new** compatibility-layer issue, please report it on this
issue. We will add it to the work-item list.

## Non-goals

- Landing inference-engine (or Mooncake Store) native-API migration in this RFC
  (that work is separate and in progress, e.g. #4070).
- Teaching applications to `installTransport` under TENT. Making the shim
  honor the classic `Transport*` contract so existing callers do not treat a
  successful TENT init as failure **is** in scope (`P1-install-transport`).
- Changing TENT runtime scheduling / failover policy.

## Work items

Priority is "if the reading holds, impact is high" — not "already on fire".

| ID | Problem | Difficulty | PR | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0-send_probe | Python `send_probe` SIGSEGV (`getMetadata()` is null) | M | #4081, follow-up #4115 | **done** |
| P0-stale-handle | Transfer failure may keep a dead peer's cached handle (`CheckSegmentStatus` was always OK) | M | #4109 | **partial** |
| P0-device-filter | `initialize(device=...)` still opened all HCAs | M | #4028 | **done** |
| P0-force-tcp | `MC_FORCE_TCP=1` / `protocol=tcp` may still select RDMA | M | #4027, follow-up #4113 | **done** |
| P0-efa-ascend | `protocol=efa\|ascend` may no-op or look successful without that transport | H | — | **open** |
| P1-sync-status | Python `transferSync` retry / `CANCELED` handling may not match TENT failover | S–M | — | **open** |
| P1-error-codes | Shim returned TENT `Status::Code` (non-negative); classic callers expect `ERR_*` | M | #4139 | **done** |
| P1-request-options | `priority` / `remote_accessible` were dropped at the shim | M | #4114 | **done** |
| P2-first-buffer | `getFirstBufferAddress` also called `getMetadata()` (same null deref as `send_probe`) | S | #4138 | **done** |
| P1-install-transport | TENT `installTransport()` returns `nullptr`; classic C/Go/EFA callers treat that as install failure | M | — | **open** |

### Residuals on landed items

These do not reopen the row, but they are not "the original hole is gone with no leftover":

- **P0-send_probe.** Python no longer dereferences `getMetadata()`. #4081 closed the segment after probing, which invalidated a handle already stored in Python `handle_map_`; #4115 stopped closing it. C++ `getMetadata()` is still `nullptr` under TENT — any remaining `getMetadata()->sendProbe` caller will still crash.
- **P0-stale-handle.** `CheckSegmentStatus` now probes via `probePeerAliveByID`. Python only calls it when **`submitTransfer` fails**. Peer death that shows up as `getTransferStatus` `FAILED` / `TIMEOUT` still leaves `handle_map_` intact. That leftover belongs with **P1-sync-status**. The unit test covers an never-opened handle, not a still-mapped handle whose RPC probe fails.
- **P0-force-tcp.** #4113 makes `forceTcp()` disable HP TCP so a config with both enabled does not fail init.
- **P1-error-codes.** Integer-returning APIs go through `tentToClassicError()`. `submitTransfer` still wraps TENT failures as `Status::Context(...)`. No in-tree test that failed on main and passed after (#4139 checklist).
- **P1-request-options.** Shim forwards `remote_accessible` → TENT perms and `TransferRequest::priority` on submit. Python `transferSync` does not set `priority` (default MEDIUM). No in-tree red/green test (#4114 checklist).

### Still open

- **P0-efa-ascend.** `init(..., protocol)` is now forwarded, but the TENT branch only special-cases `"tcp"`. `"efa"` / `"ascend"` do not pin those transports. On `USE_EFA` / `USE_CXI` Python builds, `initialize` still calls `installTransport()` after init; under TENT that returns `nullptr` and `initialize` returns `-1`. #4122 is classic TE Ascend Direct selection, not this shim item.
- **P1-sync-status.** `transferSync` still retries `numContexts()+1` times; under TENT `numContexts()` is hardcoded `1`. The poll loop handles `COMPLETED` / `FAILED` / `TIMEOUT` only — not `CANCELED` — and does not evict the cached handle on poll failure.
- **P1-install-transport.** Added from @chlins (2026-09-14). The TENT branch logs `"installTransport not used by TENT"` and returns `nullptr`. Classic contract: `nullptr` means install failed. Store already skips this via `isUsingTent()` (#2596). C / Go (`transfer_engine_c.h`) and EFA/CXI Python do not. Proposed fix A (TENT returns a non-null sentinel; in-tree callers only null-check) is preferred over gating every caller (B) or fixing only the C shim (C). Waiting on TENT owners (@alogfans) before a PR. R

items.title: [Bug] server CLI crashes on startup via bigtable adapter protobuf TypeError (load_all_adapters only catches ImportError)
items.author: ZKeeer
items.body_excerpt:
## Description

`lmcache server` (and even `lmcache server --help`) crashes on startup when the
installed `google-cloud-bigtable` is incompatible with the environment's
`protobuf` version. The crash happens during L2 adapter enumeration for the CLI
help string, before any server logic runs.

Root cause: `load_all_adapters()` only catches `ImportError`, but the bigtable
adapter's protobuf conflict raises `TypeError`, which escapes the handler and
crashes the CLI. This affects users who never use the Bigtable adapter, because
adapter enumeration is mandatory at CLI construction time.

## Environment

- lmcache: 0.5.2
- vLLM: 0.24.0
- Python: 3.12
- GPU: B200
- Model: GLM-5.2-NVFP4
- `protobuf`: >= 4.x (pulled in by vLLM/torch)
- `google-cloud-bigtable`: version requiring `protobuf<4.0` (e.g. 1.7.3)

## Reproduction

1. Install lmcache 0.5.2 in an env where `google-cloud-bigtable` resolves to a
   version requiring `protobuf<4.0` while vLLM pulls `protobuf>=4`.
2. Run `lmcache server --help` (or any server start).

## Error

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../lmcache/cli/main.py", line 30, in main
    cmd.register(subparsers)
  File ".../lmcache/cli/commands/server.py", line 58, in add_arguments
    add_storage_manager_args(parser)
  File ".../lmcache/v1/distributed/config.py", line 524, in add_storage_manager_args
    add_l2_adapters_args(parser)
  File ".../lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/config.py", line 434, in add_l2_adapters_args
    + ", ".join(sorted(get_registered_l2_adapter_types()))
  File ".../lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/config.py", line 126, in get_registered_l2_adapter_types
    return get_all_registered_names()
  File ".../lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/factory.py", line 161, in get_all_registered_names
    load_all_adapters()
  File ".../lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/factory.py", line 147, in load_all_adapters
    importlib.import_module(mod_path)
  ...
  File ".../lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/bigtable_l2_adapter.py", line 19, in <module>
    from google.cloud.bigtable.data import (
  ...
  File ".../google/cloud/bigtable_v2/proto/data_pb2.py", line 33, in <module>
    _descriptor.FieldDescriptor(
  File ".../google/protobuf/descriptor.py", line 675, in __new__
    _message.Message._CheckCalledFromGeneratedFile()
TypeError: Descriptors cannot be created directly.
If this call came from a _pb2.py file, your generated code is out of date and must be regenerated with protoc >= 3.19.0.
```

## Root cause

1. `add_l2_adapters_args` builds the `--l2-adapter` help string by calling
   `get_registered_l2_adapter_types()` (config.py:434) → `get_all_registered_names()`
   (factory.py:155) → `load_all_adapters()` (factory.py:161).
2. `load_all_adapters()` force-imports **all** pending adapter modules to list
   type names, and only catches `ImportError` (factory.py:148).
3. The bigtable adapter imports `google.cloud.bigtable` at module top
   (bigtable_l2_adapter.py:19); with an incompatible protobuf this raises
   `TypeError: Descriptors cannot be created directly` — **not** an `ImportError` —
   so it escapes the `except` and crashes the CLI.
4. #2905 introduced lazy import (`ensure_adapter_loaded`) which protects the
   runtime path, but the CLI-help path still goes through `load_all_adapters()`
   and was not protected. PR #2905's own risk note already flagged
   "CLI adapter listing" as exposed to import-time side effects / missing deps.

## Suggested fix

- **Minimal**: broaden the exception in `load_all_adapters()` (and
  `ensure_adapter_loaded()`) from `except ImportError` to `except Exception`,
  logging at debug.
- **Better**: `get_all_registered_names()` could list type names from the
  registry without force-importing all modules (true lazy listing), reserving
  imports for actual use.

## Workaround

- `export PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python`, or
- `pip install -U google-cloud-bigtable` to a version compatible with protobuf>=4.

## Notes

- `google-cloud-bigtable` is listed in `requirements/common.txt` without a
  version bound, so pip may resolve to an old release incompatible with
  protobuf 4.x/5.x.
- I could not find an existing issue for this; searched the tracker for
  "Descriptors cannot be created", "bigtable", "protobuf", "load_all_adapters".
- Bigtable adapter was introduced via #3885.

items.title: [Bug]: Grouped MLA generation kernels read out of bounds at batch > 1: the MLA generation path never sets cumSeqLensQPtr / cumSeqLensKvPtr
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

SM107, TensorRT-LLM main (C++ attention op, trtllm-gen FMHA, BF16 MLA generation with HQk 576 / HV 512, paged KV with 32 tokens per page).

### Who can help?

@farazkh80 (#15009) @pengbowang-nv

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

`AttentionOp` fills `TllmGenFmhaRunnerParams` for MLA generation (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/common/attentionOp.cpp`, the trtllm-gen MLA generation branch) with `seqLensKvPtr = params.cache_seq_lens`, but it never sets `cumSeqLensQPtr` or `cumSeqLensKvPtr`. The `SwapsAbForGen` kernels selected today do not read them, so nothing fails on main.

The grouped tokens x heads MLA generation kernels (`...VarSeqQ64Kv128{Static,Persistent}GroupedKeepsAbForGen`, selected when `FmhaOptions::mSelectsGroupedMla` is set, as #15009 proposed) do read them. With `mSelectsGroupedMla = true` and the runner parameters exactly as `AttentionOp` builds them:

- In a standalone `TllmGenFmhaRunner` microbenchmark (Kimi K3 MLA decode shape with MTP, KV length 64): batch 1 output is correct, but batch 4 and batch 16 are wrong (output sums -209.5 and -218.6, expected -243.7). Passing correct `cumSeqLensQ = [0, T, 2T, ...]` and `cumSeqLensKv = prefix sum of seqLensKv` makes all batch sizes match the non-grouped kernel.
- In serving (Kimi K3 with MTP, CUDA graphs), capture of the batch-4 graph fails with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` right after the grouped cubin is loaded. Captures of batches 5..16 happened to succeed.

#15009 only measured batch 1, where the offsets are never needed, which may be why this did not show up there.

### Expected behavior

Every kernel that the MLA generation path can select gets the metadata it reads. Either `AttentionOp` provides `cumSeqLensQPtr` / `cumSeqLensKvPtr` whenever a grouped MLA generation kernel can be selected, or the selection refuses grouped kernels when they are absent.

### actual behavior

With grouped selection enabled, batch > 1 MLA generation reads past the end of its offsets: the output is silently wrong or there is an illegal address.

### additional notes

Workaround we validated on SM107 (Kimi K3 serving, all graph batch sizes 1..16, unchanged accuracy): when grouped selection is enabled and batch > 1, `AttentionOp` launches a one-CTA kernel per MLA generation call. That kernel writes `cumSeqLensQ[i] = i * maxSeqLenQ` and `cumSeqLensKv` = the prefix sum of `cache_seq_lens` into a device buffer that is allocated before graph capture, and passes both pointers to the runner. Batch 1 skips the kernel. I can turn this into a PR together with whatever change enables grouped MLA selection, or separately behind the same switch, whichever maintainers prefer.

Related: the grouped MLA generation cubins are also registered with a mask type that does not match their names (#20376), the NVRTC fallback fails for these kernels on SM107 (#20377), and with FP8 KV the grouped E4M3 cubins hang when heads per rank do not divide 64 (#20382).

items.title: [dynamo] `not d` and `bool(d)` on a dict input add no guard on its emptiness, so the graph is reused with wrong results
items.author: peterdsharpe
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

While working on tensordict performance for PhysicsNeMo, a tensordict change (pytorch/tensordict#2634) made a compiled GLOBE training step on CPU raise a `KeyError` for an entry the model had just set (pytorch/tensordict#2648). Chasing that down the rabbit hole led me to believe that the issue is actually in Dynamo: `not d` and `bool(d)` on a dict argument add no guard on whether the dict is empty, so a graph traced with `d = {}` gets reused for a non-empty dict, and the other way round. In our case, a compiled `TensorDict(source)` that had once run with an empty dict returned an empty tensordict for every later dict. We worked around it in tensordict (pytorch/tensordict#2660), but any code that keeps `not d` or `bool(d)` as a value, instead of branching on it directly, can hit it.

I think this should be fixed because it's a silent wrong result: no error and no recompile, just the wrong branch. Expected behavior is that `not d` and `bool(d)` guard on the dict's length, as `if not d:` and `len(d) == 0` already do.

```python
import torch


def use_not(x, d):
    empty = not d
    return x + (0 if empty else 1)


def use_bool(x, d):
    nonempty = bool(d)
    return x + (1 if nonempty else 0)


def use_if(x, d):
    if not d:
        return x + 0
    return x + 1


x = torch.zeros(1)
for fn in (use_not, use_bool, use_if):
    torch._dynamo.reset()
    opt = torch.compile(fn, backend="eager", fullgraph=True)
    opt(x, {})
    print(f"{fn.__name__}: compiled {opt(x, {'a': 1}).item()}, eager {fn(x, {'a': 1}).item()}")
```

Output on 2.15.0 and nightly 2.16.0.dev20261015 (the same on 2.13.0 and 2.14.1):

```
use_not: compiled 0.0, eager 1.0
use_bool: compiled 0.0, eager 1.0
use_if: compiled 1.0, eager 1.0
```

Expected: `compiled 1.0` on all three lines.

I had an agent investigate further; below is the AI-assisted analysis.

### Error logs

None. The compiled function returns the wrong value, with no error and no recompile.

### AI-assisted analysis

An AI coding agent (Claude, in the Pi harness) ran these checks and read the Dynamo source at my request. I reviewed its findings before filing.

> With `TORCH_LOGS=guards`, the guard on `L['d']` in `use_not` and `use_bool` is only `TYPE_MATCH`; `use_if` also gets `DICT_LENGTH: not L['d']` and recompiles on the second call. `not d` is also wrong the other way round (traced with `{'a': 1}`, then called with `{}`), including when the values are tensors. It happens whether or not the code is in an inlined function, and on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14. `OrderedDict` arguments are affected as well. User-defined dict subclasses, lists, tuples and sets are guarded correctly, as is `len(d) == 0`.
>
> Possible cause, in the source of nightly 2.16.0.dev20261015: `BuiltinVariable.call_not_` (`torch/_dynamo/variables/builtin.py`) returns `len(a.items) == 0` for a `ConstDictVariable` without calling `install_dict_keys_match_guard()`, and `generic_is_true` (`torch/_dynamo/variables/object_protocol.py`, used by `bool()`) returns `bool(obj.as_python_constant())` for an empty `ConstDictVariable` without a guard. `mp_length_impl`, which `len(d)` uses, does install the guard.

items.title: [user streams] Compiled forward fails with "Fork/join stream expected a stream object at index 2" when mixing default-stream and side-stream work under autograd
items.author: aorenste
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

With autograd enabled, a function that runs some work on the default stream and
some on a side stream compiles under Inductor, but the compiled forward fails
when called:

```python
import torch

def fn(x, y):
    s = torch.Stream(device="cuda")
    a = 2 * x + y
    with s:
        b = 2 * x + y
    return a, b

x = torch.ones(2, 2, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
y = torch.ones(2, 2, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
a, b = torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True)(x, y)
b.sum().backward()
```

It works with `backend="aot_eager"`, and with Inductor when the inputs don't require grad.

#### AI-generated analysis

> The compiled forward fetches a stream for its default-stream kernels with `_get_stream_by_index(2)`, but slot 2 of the external object registry (`torch._dynamo.graph_bytecode_inputs`) holds a `torch.Event`. Registry contents at the failing call, by type: `[Stream, Stream, Event, Stream, Event, Stream]`. The events and extra streams are registered while AOT autograd inserts the backward's stream syncs. Without autograd the registry is `[Stream, Stream]`, and the forward only fetches index 1 (the side stream) and runs the default-stream kernel on the current stream.
>
> The forward graph Inductor receives has no stream annotation on the default-stream nodes (only the side-stream nodes carry `{'stream': 1}`), so the index 2 is chosen somewhere in Inductor's training-path stream handling. I haven't found where.

items.title: KV event decoder drops group_idx/medium/lora_name, breaking prefix matching for hybrid and multi-tier models
items.author: Jeffwan
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Our ZMQ decoder reads only the first four positional fields of vLLM's `BlockStored` (block_hashes, parent_block_hash, token_ids, block_size) and drops the rest. Upstream `BlockStored` (`vllm/distributed/kv_events.py`) now also carries `medium`, `lora_name`, `extra_keys`, and `group_idx`. Two of these affect correctness:

- `group_idx`: hybrid-attention models (sliding-window + full layers — Gemma, Ministral, Llama-4) hash the same token range into different KV-cache groups. Collapsing all groups into one hash space can produce false prefix matches.
- `medium`: with KV offloading, blocks live on CPU/remote tiers, but we count every block as a GPU hit, so prefix routing over-credits pods that only hold the prefix on a slower tier.

`lora_name` is also the canonical adapter id (`lora_id` is deprecated upstream); `prefix_cache.go` currently passes `loraID=-1` everywhere, so adapters aren't isolated in the index.

Relevant: `pkg/cache/kvcache/msgpack_decoder.go` (`parseEventArray`), `pkg/plugins/gateway/algorithms/prefix_cache.go`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Serve a hybrid-attention model (e.g. `google/gemma-2-9b-it`) with `--kv-events-config` enabled.
2. Send shared-prefix traffic across ≥2 replicas with the kv-event prefix router.
3. Observe requests routed to pods that don't actually have a GPU prefix hit.

### Expected behavior

Decoder parses `group_idx`/`medium`/`lora_name`; the index keys prefix entries by `(model, lora_name, group_idx)` and scores non-GPU mediums lower.

### Environment

AIBrix: main · vLLM: main (kv-events enabled).

items.title: [Feature]: Support NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming (nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b)
items.author: robin-bially
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

NVIDIA recently released **Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming** ([nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b)), a 600M-parameter multilingual streaming ASR model under the OpenMDW-1.1 license.

Key features:
- **Native streaming architecture** with Cache-Aware FastConformer-RNNT, supporting configurable chunk sizes from 80ms to 1120ms
- **35 languages** (19 transcription-ready + 13 broad-coverage + 8 adaptation-ready), including German, English, French, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, etc.
- **Automatic language detection** via `target_lang=auto`
- **Punctuation & capitalization** built-in
- On a single H100: **240 concurrent streams at 80ms chunk**, ~17x more than Parakeet RNNT 1.1B

This would be a great addition to vLLM's supported ASR models, complementing the existing Voxtral Realtime and Qwen3-ASR support. The model is already available in HuggingFace Transformers (`AutoModelForRNNT`) and NVIDIA NeMo.

### Alternatives

Currently, the only open-source streaming ASR options in vLLM are:
- **Voxtral Realtime (4B)** — high VRAM due to persistent encoder KV-cache, limiting concurrent streams
- **Qwen3-ASR (0.6B/1.7B)** — segment-based (5s chunks), higher latency

Nemotron 3.5 would fill the gap for a lightweight, truly native streaming model with low latency and high throughput.

### Additional context

- HuggingFace: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b
- Architecture: FastConformer-CacheAware-RNNT with language-ID prompt conditioning
- Primary framework: NeMo, with Transformers support added
- Release date: June 4, 2026

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Perf/Feature] KDA decode: recurrent path 4.2–5.7x behind vendored Triton at the 64-head geometry; fused ops reject H=64; fp32 state crashes instead of raising
items.author: brandonfzhang
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

Three stacked problems keep FlashInfer's KDA family out of GLM-5.3 serving:

1. **Perf:** at GLM-5.3's per-rank decode geometry (H=64, T=1), FI's recurrent KDA
   (`cute-dsl`, run with its documented bf16 state) is **4.2–5.7x behind** the
   frameworks' kernels (vLLM's vendored fla Triton / FlashKDA) at every batch size.
2. **Eligibility:** FI's *fused* KDA decode ops reject the 64-head count outright,
   so the fast path never applies at this geometry (it wins at the Kimi-K3 head
   counts, where FI leads 1.13x decode / 1.22x chunk-prefill).
3. **Contract:** both serving frameworks keep **fp32** KDA state pools. Feeding
   fp32 state to FI's decode produces a misleading crash signature instead of a
   dtype error, which is part of why no framework integrates the FI family at all
   (four distinct non-FI KDA implementations ship across vLLM/SGLang today).

## Environment

- NVIDIA GB300 (SM103); CUDA 13.0; FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5
- Timing: CUPTI, 20 interleaved rounds, SM clock locked 2070 MHz, fp64 gates
- Geometry from the published GLM-5.3 GB300 recipes (TP2/TP4 shards → H=64/rank)

## Exact call parameters

KDA recurrent decode: `num_heads=64`, `num_v_heads=64`, `d_k=128`, `d_v=128`,
`T=1` token per sequence, bf16 q/k/v with bf16 recurrent state (FI's documented
contract; the frameworks hold fp32 state). Batch varies below.

## Measurements — H=64, T=1 decode step (µs)

| batch | vLLM recurrent (fla Triton) | FlashKDA packed | FI recurrent (cute-dsl) | FI behind |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.6 | 3.5 | 20.0 | 5.7x |
| 8 | 14.0 | 15.5 | 47.3 | 3.4x |
| 32 | 44.1 | 50.7 | 183.0 | 4.2x |
| 128 | 167.9 | 186.0 | 771.4 | 4.6x |

(`fi_auto` matches `cute-dsl` within noise, so this is the best FI has at H=64.)

## Ask

1. Whitelist H=64 in the fused KDA decode ops (or document why it is excluded) —
   GLM-5.3's shard geometry lands exactly there.
2. Make the recurrent path competitive at H=64/T=1, or route it to the fused
   kernels once (1) lands.
3. Raise a clear dtype error on fp32 decode state instead of crashing; better,
   accept fp32 state — it is what both frameworks' state pools hold, and it is the
   single biggest adoption blocker for the FI KDA family even where FI already wins
   (Kimi-K3 geometry).

## Related

- #6485 (CAKE packed KDA training kernels — forward/backward, ragged)

items.title: [Perf][SM103] MSA sparse prefill: runtime scales with prefix length instead of queries x top-k — ~18 ms flat at a 64K prefix, 113x behind Triton on chunk-append
items.author: brandonfzhang
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

On MiniMax-M3's MSA sparse prefill (top-k 16 blocks of 128, fp8-e4m3 KV),
FlashInfer's MSA prefill kernel costs **~17.9 ms whenever the attended prefix is
65536 tokens — regardless of how many queries the call carries** (512 or 16384).
With top-k sparsity each query touches at most 16x128 = 2048 KV positions, so a
512-query call has no business costing milliseconds: the in-tree Triton sparse
kernel does the same call in 157 µs (**113x**). On fresh sequences (prefix 0) the
same FI kernel is fine — it *beats* that Triton kernel 1.6–2.8x at large q — so the
pathology is specifically whatever work scales with prefix length.

Related route-level finding: FI's E4M3-KV route is a median ~5.9x slower than FI's
own bf16-KV route on identical shapes, and the fp8 cache is what this model serves.

## Environment

- NVIDIA GB300 (SM103); CUDA 13.0; FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5 (identical times at both FI
  versions we ran; the serve-pinned 0.6.x wheels ship no msa_ops at all)
- Timing: CUPTI, 20 interleaved rounds, SM clock locked 2070 MHz, fp64 gates
- Shapes from live-serve captures of the published MiniMax-M3 GB300 recipes

## Exact call parameters

MSA sparse prefill: `num_q_heads=16`, `num_kv_heads=1`, `head_dim=128`, top-k 16,
`block_size=128`, indexer 1 head x 128 dim, KV `float8_e4m3fn`, `batch=1` varlen.
Rows vary `per_seq_q` (queries in the call) and `prefix_len` (already-cached
tokens the selection runs over).

## Measurements (µs)

| per_seq_q | prefix_len | FI msa prefill | in-tree Triton sparse | FI vs Triton |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 8 | 0 | 76.8 | 13.2 | 5.8x behind |
| 8192 | 0 | 1247.3 | 3481.6 | **2.8x ahead** |
| 16384 | 0 | 2358.9 | 3708.4 | **1.6x ahead** |
| 8 | 65536 | 17842.9 | 157.3 | **113x behind** |
| 8192 | 65536 | 16996.6 | 3960.3 | 4.3x behind |
| 16384 | 65536 | 18226.8 | 3962.1 | 4.6x behind |

The FI column at prefix 65536 is flat (~17–18 ms) across a 2048x range of query
counts. (A second rival, the SGLang fused sparse FMHA, leads everything at large q
— 713 µs at the heaviest row — but the prefix-flat behavior is the FI-side bug.)

## Ask

1. Make MSA prefill cost scale with queries x top-k, not prefix length — whatever
   per-call work walks the full prefix (selection re-processing, metadata build,
   or a dense pass) dominates the chunk-append regime that chunked prefill runs.
2. Close the E4M3-KV vs bf16-KV route gap (median ~5.9x on identical shapes) —
   the fp8 cache regime is the one production uses.

## Related

- #6020 (packed-FP8 MSA sparse decode for MiniMax-M3, SM100/SM103 — experimental)

items.title: [Feature]: prims_ts dense paged decode: allow FP8-E4M3 Q/KV with BF16 output
items.author: zyongye
items.body_excerpt:
### Before submitting - [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet. ### Problem The prims_ts dense paged decode path accepts FP8-E4M3 Q with FP8-E4M3 K/V only when the output is FP16 or FP8. BF16 output is rejected. Checked on **v0.7.1** and **v0.7.2** (`d84335d`); `main` has the same code. ``` NotImplementedError: attention-ts decode supports FP16->FP16, BF16->BF16, FP8-E4M3->FP16, and FP8-E4M3->FP8-E4M3; BF16 Q + FP8 K/V, BF16/FP8-E4M3 Q + NVFP4 K/V, and BF16 Q/K + FP8 V; got Q_torch.float8_e4m3fn_K_torch.float8_e4m3fn_V_torch.float8_e4m3fn->torch.bfloat16 ``` Two checks restrict FP8 Q → BF16 output to the QToken-KvBlock sparse route (links are to v0.7.2): 1. [`_validate_dtype_pair`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L695-L748) allows it only with `allow_fp8_bf16_output=True`. Only the sparse route sets that flag: [`allow_fp8_bf16_output=use_q_token_kv_block_sparse_route`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L3431-L3437), with `use_q_token_kv_block_sparse_route=True` passed only from `q_token_kv_block_sparse_metadata.py`. Every dense entry point rejects BF16: | dense entry point | where it rejects FP8 Q/KV → BF16 | |---|---| | `BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper.plan` | [decode.py:3875](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L3875), **only when `validate=True`** | | `batch_decode_with_paged_kv_cache` (no `workspace_buffer`) | `get_prims_ts_batch_decode_workspace_size`, [decode.py:2054](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L2054) | | `prepare_prims_ts_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` | `_prepare_prims_ts_batch_decode_plan(use_q_token_kv_block_sparse_route=False)`, [decode.py:3431](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L3431-L3437) | 2. [`FmhaDecodeConfig.supports_reduction_dtypes`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/kernels/fmha_decode/fmha_decode_config.py#L1275-L1290) returns False for FP8 Q → BF16 output unless `uses_q_token_kv_block_sparse_page_route` is set. This check doesn't raise. When it fails, the automatic policy drops the cluster SMEM reduction. So a caller whose activations are BF16 has to request FP16 and run a separate FP16 → BF16 cast after every attention call. **Results.** GB300, B=4, 4 query tokens per request, 16 Q heads, 1 KV head, head_dim 128, page 128, KV length 4096, dense mask. Each mode ran in a fresh process, because `_resolve_decode_launch_spec` is `functools.cache`d. v0.7.1 and v0.7.2 give identical numbers. | mode | planned config | rel. error vs FP32 ref | rel. diff vs FP16 output | time (CUDA-graph replay, CUDA events, warm L2) | |---|---|--:|--:|--:| | FP16 output (supported today) | `splits_kv=6`, cluster SMEM reduction | 2.504e-2 | — | | | FP16 output + cast to BF16 (current workaround) | | | | 10.42 µs | | BF16 output, `plan(validate=False)`, no patch (`--no-validate`) | `splits_kv=8`, no cluster SMEM reduction | 2.523e-2 | 2.03e-2 | 7.96 µs | | BF16 output, only `_validate_dtype_pair` relaxed (`--relax-pair-only`) | `splits_kv=8`, no cluster SMEM reduction | 2.523e-2 | 2.03e-2 | 7.96 µs | | BF16 output, both checks relaxed (`--relax`) | `splits_kv=6`, cluster SMEM reduction | 2.513e-2 | 2.36e-3 | **7.35 µs** | - **Accuracy:** every BF16 row has the same error vs the FP32 reference as FP16 output, about 2.5e-2. That error comes from the FP8 inputs. - **Both checks relaxed:** the BF16 plan matches the FP16 plan, and the output differs from FP16 output only by BF16 rounding (2.4e-3). It takes 7.35 µs vs 10.42 µs for the workaround. - **`validate=False` is inconsistent:** `BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper.plan(validate=False)` already builds and runs FP8 → BF16 with no patch. The dtype check is skipped, but `supports_reduction_dtypes` still fails, so the policy falls back to 8 splits without the cluster SMEM reduction. On this entry point the dtype check only applies under `validate=True`, and with `validate=False` the reduction check quietly gives a slower plan. Relaxing only `_validate_dtype_pair` gives the same result, so both checks need to change together. - **Wider sweep:** at B = 1–64, with the same heads, page size, KV length and timing method, relaxing both checks saved 3.3–3.9 µs per call against FP16 output + cast. The difference from FP16 output stayed at 1.4e-3 to 2.8e-3. **Related:** #5720 relaxes the same two checks for FP8 Q with NVFP4 K/V → BF16 on the dense route. It also adds `test_attention_ts_decode_fp8_kv_bf16_output_remains_route_scoped`, which asserts that FP8 K/V → BF16 stays rejected outside the sparse route. If that restriction is deliberate, could you share the reason? At this shape, the dense kernels pick the same plan and give the same accuracy as with FP16 output once both checks are relaxed.
Minimal reproduction (repro_fp8_bf16_out.py) ```python """prims_ts dense paged decode: FP8-E4M3 Q/KV -> BF16 output is rejected. python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py # FP16 output works, BF16 raises python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --relax # relax both dtype gates python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --relax-pair-only # relax _validate_dtype_pair only python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --no-validate # plan(validate=False), no patch """ import argparse import functools import torch from flashinfer.attention.prims_ts import BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper B, SQ, HQ, HKV, D, PAGE, KV_LEN = 4, 4, 16, 1, 128, 128, 4096 FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn def relax_gates(reduction=True): import flashinfer.attention.prims_ts.decode as dec from flashinfer.attention.prims_ts.kernels.fmha_decode import ( fmha_decode_config as cfg, ) validate = dec._validate_dtype_pair @functools

items.title: [Roadmap]Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon
items.author: liusy58
items.body_excerpt:
# [Roadmap] Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon 
@liusy58 @QiuMike @alexnails 
Phase 1 landed in #27139 — a per-rank daemon holds post-quantized weights and serves them over CUDA IPC; weight load drops from ~306–327s to <1s on Qwen3-235B FP8 ([blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-21-sglang-fast-recovery)). This issue tracks the next steps. Contributions and feedback are welcome.

Related: #27052 (Fast Recovery framework), #27310 (GPU Memory Service / VMM)

Goals: <10s cold restart and <1s warm standby switch; broaden model & quant coverage; make the cache outlive the daemon; make resident weights usable beyond the one GPU they sit on.

Where Phase 1 stands: TP + PP, single-node and multi-node launch (each node spawns its share of ranks and joins one dist group), zero-copy IPC per GPU, unquantized + block-wise FP8. Not yet: cross-node daemon coordination / failover, DP & EP shard keying, spec-decoding draft models, weight update / sleep-wake, cache surviving daemon death.

## Model & quantization coverage

- [ ] parity harness — disk-load vs daemon-load `state_dict` diff (names / shape / dtype / stride / byte hash) + short GSM8K gate; required evidence for every new allowlist entry
- [ ] carry post-processing metadata in the manifest (final shape/stride, layout tag, whitelisted module attrs) instead of reproducing `process_weights_after_loading` on a meta-init model — this is what blocks most quant methods today
- [ ] quant methods: per-tensor fp8 / w8a8 int8 / mxfp8 / nvfp4 / compressed-tensors / awq / gptq-marlin #32398 
- [ ] archs: MoE (DeepSeek V3/V4, Ling, Kimi K3) / hybrid linear attention / multimodal (vision tower + projector) / LoRA base weights https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33684
- [ ] MTP & EAGLE draft models (per-rank draft daemon), removing the `--speculative-algorithm` rejection in `server_args.py` #32744
- [ ] generic post-map rebuild hook to replace the hardcoded `_rebuild_stale_views`; make tied storages, param→buffer flips and non-persistent buffers explicit in the manifest
- [ ] publish the support matrix in docs; unsupported combinations keep hard-erroring (no silent wrong numerics)

## Transport: CUDA VMM shareable handles (#27310 §4.2)



- [ ] `vmm_fd` backend (skeleton already in `weight_cache/transport.py`): `cuMemCreate` + FD handles over `SCM_RIGHTS`, VA reservation on import, `torch_ipc` stays the fallback, `--weight-cache-transport {auto,torch_ipc,vmm_fd}` #33279
- [ ] `mooncake` backend https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36293


## Weight update without reload

- [ ] epoch handoff on stable VAs: readers unmap → writer commits → readers remap at the same VAs, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid
- [ ] daemon as the weight delivery agent for trainer pushes (NCCL/RDMA); un-gate the `update_weights_*` rejections in `weight_updater.py`
- [ ] colocated RL: engine itself takes the writer role, same protocol, no daemon in the loop

## Multi-instance & cross-GPU sharing

- [ ] key the cache by physical GPU UUID + config fingerprint (plus optional `--weight-cache-namespace`) under a configurable runtime dir. Today the socket is `/tmp/sglang_weight_cache_rank{global_rank}.sock`, so 2× tp=4 on one 8-GPU node collide and rank 0 of the second instance attaches to the GPU 0 daemon
- [ ] discovery: replace static socket paths with a lightweight registry (file-based dir, optionally etcd) so an engine rank selects a daemon by `CacheConfig` match rather than by process rank, and locates daemons across nodes without a manual `--weight-cache-socket`
- [ ] `--weight-cache-peer-copy` — when no daemon holds the shard on the local GPU, `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` it from a peer-GPU daemon (NVLink-domain check, chunked on a low-priority stream, bandwidth cap so a serving neighbour is not disturbed). 1× memory per instance, sub-second over NVLink vs ~300s from disk
- [ ] preference order local zero-copy > peer copy > disk, reported per rank
- [ ] fleet fill: a daemon fills itself from a peer daemon instead of disk (P2P on-node, NCCL/RDMA cross-node), so a fleet cold start pays one disk read per shard group — the real bottleneck for 1T+ models on shared FS; align with the checkpoint-engine broadcast path
- [ ] out of scope for now: resharding across TP/EP topologies (tp=4 daemon → tp=8 engine)

## Multi-node, DP & EP

- [ ] primary–secondary daemon coordination for multi-node TP (e.g. TP=16 = 2 nodes × 8 GPUs): primary orchestrates daemon startup, cross-node NCCL process-group formation and readiness signalling; secondaries load their local shards in parallel and serve IPC handles to engines on their own node. Basic multi-node launch already works via `--nnodes/--node-rank/--dist-init-method`; what is missing is the cluster state machine
- [ ] cross-node daemon lifecycle: primary tracks which secondaries are alive, triggers coordinated restarts, signals engines on a dead secondary's node to fall back to disk; promote a secondary when the primary dies
- [ ] DP support: every DP rank on a GPU maps the same daemon's handles, so a model is read from disk and quantized exactly once per GPU regardless of DP degree (today each DP rank disk-loads independently). This is about supporting SGLang's DP deployment model, not cross-GPU sharing
- [ ] EP support: expert shards differ per EP rank, so cache and key them by `ep_rank`; handle partial expert loading when a rank owns a subset of experts
- [ ] `CacheConfig`: add `ep_rank`, `dp_rank` and `node_rank` for correct shard identification under EP and multi-node (`dp_size`/`ep_size` are already there)

## Ops & reliability

- [ ] `daemon status` command + Prometheus metrics (resident bytes, attached clients, load time, hit / mismatch / fallback), and an engine endpoint reporting how each rank got its weights
- [ ] runtime dir with owner-only permissions + `SO_PEERCRED` check before handing out handles (no world-writable `/tmp` sockets)
- [ ] `protocol_version` in the handshake with a documented skew policy (the env stamp alrea
